title: Shuko
history: In 2005, Sushi Chefs Nick Kim and Jimmy Lau met while working at Masa. Shuko was born in 2013, and it is where the combined vision of both chefs is executed daily, in the form of omakase and kaiseki menus. That vision is one that veers away from the norm of high-end, sushi establishments -- both in terms of the chefs' innovative use of ingredients and the hip atmosphere dictated in part by the popular music that pervades the dining room. And if a three-star NYT review is any indicator, it succeeds quite well.

reviews.review:
I hate to say it but SHUKO was a huge miss.  .  It was a bit weird experience from start to finish.  Servers were kind, if a bit over-attentive (we did go on an off night (monday) but we were literally the only diners the whole time - think they closed the restaurant after we left).  

The food was really the problem-- NOTHING stood out or had that deep flavorful or eye opening moment to justify the price.  They hit the trendy "expensive" ingredients like wagyu, toro, uni--but without creativity or anything that would justify the price.  The milk bread/ caviar course was good, but nothing else gave that kind of experience.  It felt disappointingly ordinary.

Would hope shuko would re-think their menu entirely and maybe offer diners some more surprises/ excitement if they hope to keep competing in a city where every other day a new sushi temple is launched.

this place has such a weird vibe. like tell me why they were playing jeremiah and other hip hop artists in a what's supposed to be a romantic upscale atmosphere 

also the bar seating is a bit cramped. helps that they check ur jackets for u. 

i was super full by the end but loved the dessert the most. everything was very balanced and thought out in terms of flavor and texture so i really enjoyed but def come hungry!!!!

By far the most expensive yet fulfilling experience at a restaurant that I have ever had. As soon as you walk in its breath taking from start to finish. Went in for my girlfriend (now wife) birthday and was sooo good. They even wrote a card wishing her a happy  birthday. It just kept coming ! the food felt like it would not stop (i think 30 dishes - this was pre covid). Every bite was a amazing (the range and different styles was an explosion of taste) . Once in a life time dining experience as the price is quite high. ice cream was amazing  and home made!. Apps and the fish were beyond this taste realm. Service was immaculate. Everything down to the table setting and utensils was spot on. If i were to open a restaurant this would be it.

What a meal!! I was treated to it so I didn't have to pay the high price tag but it was delightful. The service was amazing. Each dish was carefully prepared. We upgraded the toast to include more toro, Uni and caviar. Wow. There were 16 pieces and dessert. I loved it all. I will remember this meal for quite some time. It's a small place and feels intimate. The door isn't marked. Like a speakeasy! Highly recommend this if you love sushi.

This place has declined a bit over the years. The omakase is fine, but truly not that memorable (can't remember a single thing I had that stood out?). What's really disappointing is the wait and the service level. We had a reservation on a week night and didn't get seated until ~45 mins later. Guys, we have to work the next day to afford these prices! When I expressed to the host that we were running very late, she just shrugged. At these price point, that's not the right answer. Please do better.

At $270 a person, this omakase was good but nothing that really stood out. The whole experience was about a 3.7stars. The most exceptional part of the meal was the service and ambiance. 

The nigiri itself was about average. There were a couple pieces that were really fishy and I didn't really enjoy it much. I feel like the nigiri itself was a bit on the smaller side as well. The rice was perfectly seasoned though. I really enjoyed the caviar/ tuna appetizer that was served with Japanese milk bread toast. It was flavorful and in my opinion was one of the most balanced courses  out of our entire meal. Our last sushi piece was a handroll that consisted of pickled cucumbers and shiso leaf. I would've preferred to end the meal with a different piece as the shiso and pickle was such a strong flavor, I felt like all the built up to this last piece was disappointing. Most omakase places tend to build up to pieces that are stronger and richer in flavor so this was quite the opposite. The barley ice cream with sea salt and rice crackers was a perfect way to end the night though.

Service itself was exceptional. The staff was super attentive and constantly folding napkins/ refilling waters/etc. 

This place is perfect for a romantic date/ anniversary dinner. Unfortunately my date took me as a first date when I wasn't even hungry so I felt like I couldn't truly appreciate the vibe. On top of that, their price listed on Resy was about half of the bill we received so we were in for a shock.  

If you're going to impress someone, this is the place to go. If you're going for food, there are probably better options out there.
I don't care about rice and Shuko is known for its Sushi rice. All I can think about is their rice. Go to Shuko to experience this rice. The rice is an experience in its own right.
Spectacular food. The chef did a great job with the food. Great selection of Japanese beers. The servers were rude, but that didn't completely negate the food experience.

Bomb diggity! This was my second time here. While I ate with a friend the first time, the second occasion was eating solo.
While the food is not inexpensive, it lives up to the hype. Sushi is fresh and the service is attentive and educational. Both the sommelier and the sushi chef did a great job in walking me though the menu and guiding me meal.

If there is one hill I am willing to die on, it's that omakase is an industry plant. Unless it's an ultra special occasion, why on God's green earth would you spend $270 per person for sushi? I know $270 is upscale omakase, but still why would you pay $130 a head? The sum of the parts just don't add up, and there is no way you're going to like everything the chef gives you... I mean if you're paid like that no shade. I'm not pocket watching don't worry.

We decided to hit Shuko ($270 a head) for a work celebration. Not my choice, obviously. Upon arriving, the only thing that denotes it is the restaurant is a cute little yellow flower right by the door. As the door swings open, you enter a beautiful, authentically Japanese space with an elongated bar with some classic hip hop hits playing faintly through the speakers.

We were walked to our seats at the counter and this is one of those places where they push in your chairs for you like you are a little kid. But at $270 a head I was letting them do all that lol. Weeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee!

The $270 show began, as the chef whipped out his Kiritsuke Blue Steel knife and began cutting this fish like he was a world class samurai in the Sengoku Period. He is honestly an artist. Art takes many forms, but this has to be right up there with the best of them.

Caviar is so overrated to me, but this caviar on top of toro tartare with a small piece of milk bread made me eat my words. It actually had me audibly saying "OH MY GOD."

As the rest of the sushi came piece by piece, it was undeniably phenomenal with the standouts being that piece of fatty tuna along with the wagyu. But I mean at $270 a head it better be phenomenal. $270 a head before drinks... for $270 I could probably buy some..... nvm.

Before I wrap this up, I need to shoutout my boy Salvador as he was keeping my plate of ginger FULL. At places like this I always try to get as much ginger as possible, as I need my get-back. $270 on me? Well Imma eat my body weight in ginger. My guy Salvador would not let my ginger plate be empty. Y'all need to give Salvador a raise!!

In closing, I hear you: "But Johnny, if you loved it so much how is it an industry plant?" Great question, my dear reader. Easy answer:

Was this experience worth $240 more than a platter of sushi from 295 Mercer or a Trust Me from Sugarfish? Absolutely not. Not even close... but I guess if you really want to flex up on somebody or you have an unlimited bankroll, then why not come here?

Splurged here for an anniversary dinner. At $270/pp without drinks, tip, and tax, it is pretty pricy but so worth it. Each pair gets their own omakase chef. The cuts of fish are amazing. Each one has special sauce and is absolutely spectacular. This is the best omakase in the city, hands down. Drinks are great too. Music is hip hop and fun to listen to.

I was expecting the seating I requested to be accommodated. It wasn't. When I asked for the manager, the girl who approached me was incredibly rude, and had a serious attitude. Tall girl, skinny, teeth like horse. Clearly no people skills. It was quite obvious she's either new, or had never done this type of work before. 

Food was overpriced, and nothing special. 

Music was loud and inconsistent. Poor taste, whoever chose it. 

Won't be back. Especially after how that manager conducted herself.

This is my favorite omakase sushi spot in NYC! Their toro tartare with caviar on milkbread is mouthwatering... seriously, I dream about this dish at night! The staff is always friendly and welcoming. Fish is super fresh and all their ingredients are top-of-the-line in quality. Their plum sake is also delicious!

Service was great.  Nice atmosphere. Food left something to be desired. Went with my husband and the bill for omakase with alcohol pairing came to $1200. I left feeling underwhelmed and overcharged. So many omakase are have the price and twice as good.

I was a SHUKO raver when it first opened. It was beautiful. The sushi was different and special.  But Mr Kim now disappoints.  The sushi is very underwhelming.  For $270 omakase we should demand better.  I'm going to have to look for a replacement. I'm sorry   I used to regale them but this is my second mediocre omakase. I'm done.

I think the place has lost a bit of its luster since it opened 7-8 years ago. The hype and originality has passed and now it's a place for bankers and those that want to be seen. Having said that, the quality of the fish is still high, the portions are generous, and we thoroughly enjoyed the wine list and sake we ordered. 

For those looking for a more traditional omakase experience, I'd recommend elsewhere like Ginza Onodera or Kanoyama. The ordering of the nigiri was also unconventional as well: they served toro early on in the meal when heavier pieces are usually saved for last. 

This place is fun, the toro + caviar toast is delicious, and it's a more laid back place versus stuffy traditional edomae sushi places. Best to take your gringo friends who can't tell the difference . Multiple sushi chefs churning out nigiri, so there won't be too much pleasantries. 

The bill will set you back, but you'll leave having a great time. Music is on point.

Experience was mixed. But before I get to the review, who lets a dog sit at a sushi bar?

Yes, an actual dog. Sitting on a customer's lap at the sushi bar. Next to the fish. Prime time Friday night. At a $270/head omakase. I honestly have no words. I saw the customers arrive with their pup and give the hostess a hard time, but I never imagined they'd let them in. Isn't that a serious health violation?

Ok now the rest. The good: We really enjoyed our sushi courses. It was not so memorable as the last time we dined here, when it was half the price. But there were some standout bites.

The bad: we really did not enjoy the first few courses - the sunomono, the sashimi, the toro tartare were forgettable. Service was mixed. The sushi chef and sommelier were wonderful but the waitress existed purely to upsell us.

All in all a pleasant evening but not worth the price tag. And the dog thing really got to me - if no one blinked an eye at that, what else do they let slide?

Had an outstanding experience at Shuko. The food was delicious (literally every course was great) and the service was attentive and polite. Nice ambiance with good music playing in the background. Love getting to watch the chefs at work. 

Losing a star because I do think it's a bit overpriced- could probably get a similar quality experience for much less elsewhere in NYC. However, no complaints about the overall experience. I recommend it if you're looking to splurge for an occasion!

I took my family for omakase last year while I was in town after seeing Shuko featured on David Chang's Hulu special. Love the unassuming environment and overall it was a nice experience. My only grievance was that I noticed my neighboring patrons had a course with gold flakes, so I asked our chef if there were different levels of omakase and he replied "no". Do I pointed out discreetly and politely and told him I saw the gold flake course featured on the show like how the folks next to us was being served. So I found out he skipped the gold flakes for us and subbed it and I felt like it was assumed we wouldn't know the difference. He felt bad and "gave" us an extra course without gold flakes but for me it ruined my expectations. I didn't make it noticeable to my family because I didn't want to take away from their experience. 
I would still recommend this to try but personally I wouldn't come back because I felt mistreated in that moment. Otherwise host, wait staff, presentation was great.

This place was incredible! One of the best omakase I've ever had in my life! My friend surprised me and took me here for my birthday. We sat at the sushi bar and everything about this place was impeccable. The vibe is nice, cozy, intimate, and hip. I'd say the interior is very minimalist and they were playing really good 90s hip hop at the perfect volume. The chopstick holders had a lot of character, every seat had a s different design- super cute! 

Onto the chef and the omakase.. it was unbelievable in the best possible way. Every piece that our chef made for us was mouthwatering. Every single bite was delicious and very memorable. My favorite was the uni, ikura, hokkaido, toro, wagyu, and the caviar dish. Every piece tasted so fresh and bursted with flavor.

Had the Albarino wine- wow! It paired so nicely with every dish and the wine tasted excellent. 

Let's talk service- one of the best service I've experienced. They were very attentive, but not overbearing in anyway. Always made sure everything was perfect and the best part was that they had a little birthday dessert for me with a handwritten card- I wanted to cry from happiness lol. Everything about this place exceeded beyond my expectations!

Would I recommend? Absooolutely! 11 out of 10! I will definitely be back! 

Note: the door has no sign on it besides the address number on the side which is easy to miss. I walked passed it twice lol. And I'd recommend sitting at the sushi bar- it's cool to watch the chefs in their element.
Completely overpriced meh experience from a supposedly one of the best omakase in NYC. It felt more like a casual local bar with some mediocre sushi. I wouldn't go again.

Good lord, this is one the best Omakase I have ever had.  It's slightly on the pricey side at $270 a person, but every piece of fish was really outstanding.  I sat at the sushi bar and the meal took 1:45 or so.  I had a $12 Japanese lager with my meal.  They have an excellent selection of Japanese whiskies, but those prices match the food price and I don't love paying $25 to $100 for an ounce of whiskey no matter how good it is.

My favorite pieces were as follows:
1. Chutoro
2. Wagyu
3. Barracuda
4. Horse Mackerel
5. Scallop
6. Salmon Roe

Many other good pieces but those were my favorites.  

Service was impeccable and they kept the fresh house made ginger coming (I ate 4 servings of this).

The small bite of ice cream at the end was a nice palate cleanser.

One other thing, there is no sign on the door and I walked past it twice trying to find it.  That's just part of the adventure I guess.

Absolutely amazing experience.  I've been fortunate enough to go here twice now and it's a surreal food experience.  Each dish is masterfully crafted into edible art that pleases the eyes and touches your soul via your taste buds.

Was here last evening for a Sushi/Saki/Wine pairing business dinner.  Truly an amazing experience.  Interacting with the sushi chefs who are working with you 3' away was amazing.  I loved seeing the box of goodies that the check was workign with.  No plastic wrapped fish in a freezer case here, some of the most beautiful fish I've ever seen, and eaten.  Highly recommended, will be back.
The best sushi on the east coast. Unbelievably good. Would give more stars if I could across the board: Food, service, environment. All 12/10.

$50 for a 1/4 whiskey? Asked the bartender to do a proper pour and he responded that they will be charging double for a "double" shot. 

On top of having TERRIBLE seating next to a wall which is right next to the entrance (I had requested bar seating)

He decided to get the manager but I didn't wait, there's no need to wait. Your bartender decided that instead of just pouring a PROPER hand, that they wanted to charge double for the other portion that was already supposed to be in there. Your bartender decided to sacrifice a $500+ bill to save a little whiskey. I wish I took a photo of it before he took the glass away. 

I would fire this guy if he were running my bar.

Btw, you're not the best sushi place in the village, you're just closest to my office. 

Officially on my never return list. 



0/10

My girlfriend and I celebrated our anniversary here, and it was the best omakase either of us had ever had. We sat at the counter, and the experience was nothing short of magical.

Every piece of sushi was a masterpiece, and it felt like a privilege to be able to watch the chef in their element. We did the drink pairing too, and every drink was indeed a perfect match for the dish it was served with.

The ambiance was superb, as was the service. The other guests also seemed to be having a great time!

All in all, I'd highly recommend Shuko. It's a unique and worthwhile experience, and I'll definitely be going back.

There is no other better sushi!  Every single bite was heavenly good! We are spoiled with fresh seafood in the PNW but Shuko has left a deep impression with us! Until the next time we are in the Big Apple, thank you to the staff of Shuko and Al for taking care of us!  Btw it's a little hidden so it's added a little thrilling to our experience!

Celebrated my friends birthday here. We got a private room downstairs and omakase. Food was high quality, my favourite was the toro and the caviar on milk bread. However, I didn't think it was worth the price. Service was meh, the servers were friendly but weren't super interactive and our whole meal took almost 4 hours so they were a bit slow.

Hands down one of the best omakase I've had... you MUST sit at the counter seating to see the magic happen. 

The price is steep ($270 for the omakase, with the option to add extra sushi or uni toppings for $$$), but the chefs are so generous with the fish portions that it's worth every dollar spent. Some of the freshest fish I've ever had the pleasure of tasting: standouts include the Hokkaido uni (sweet, juicy, bursting with flavor), chu-toro (melts in your mouth), and the striped Jack (such an interesting texture and flavor profile). The caviar + toro tartare starter was also so fun. 

We shared a small sake bottle, but you definitely don't need additional drinks to have an amazing time here. Chefs are super friendly and professional. Would totally come again after I save up for another round
Unbelievable. Incredible music. The toro was the best ive ever had. The caviar toast was ridiculous. Sit at the bar and enjoy the chefs hard work. Will be back very soon.
Omakase left me leaving stuffed! Thank you for a great time. First time receiving a hand written card from a restaurant to celebrate my birthday  thank you!

Came here yesterday for dinner and was running late due to the parade nearby luckily the staff was very understanding we were a group of 4 and ordered omakase.. it's alot of food and we really struggled to finish the last two peices (toro hand roll and the cucumber peice ) the soy sauce ice cream was different and my friends liked the rice cracker sprinkles it came with.. The peices were okay but none of them really stood out to me... and for that price I expected to be wowed. We could tell our chef wasn't the head chef and his knife skills weren't on par with some of the other chefs. The music was a tad bit too loud that we couldn't hear the chef tell us the name of the fish..However the waiters were attentive and refilled our water consistently. The bill came out to $1400 for four people not sure why they charged for green tea for 3 when only one person asked for it for themselves and they brought it at the end when we couldn't even drink or eat anymore..

Celebrated my boyfriend's birthday here and felt it was great, but not worth the price. 

To start, the Toki-yo old fashioned and Satsuma sunrise cocktails were great. 

As for the omakase, it was perfectly fine, though I do think this spot is a little expensive compared to some other spots - and boy, is the competition in NYC at an all-time high right now. 

Vibe and service were fantastic. Sushi birthday card at the end was a nice touch!

4.5 stars.

Attentive service from the waitstaff. But it was nonexistent where it matters most--from the chef.

Once our chef began plating the fish, he would set it down without a word and walk away. Neither he nor the other servers explained what exactly my friend and I were eating until we asked. I've had omakase before. The courses are named as they are presented to you.

If the chef or the server isn't going to tell you what you're eating, why bother going?

This is part two of my 30th Birthday Dinner from my wonderful girlfriend. We came to NYC for a little getaway trip. My girlfriend arranged 2 omakase dinners for me. The first one was at Sushi by Bou and the other was Shuko. We wanted to try an upscale omakase and compare it to a casual omakase to see if there were any differences.

We went with the seasonal Omakase menu which was $228 per person and the beverage tasting which was $125 per person.

Ambiance - 4/5 -The door getting into the restaurant was private with no numbers or signs directing you to get in. We just assumed it was a random door on the street which made the experience a little thrilling. The ambiance inside was a classic upscale omakase restaurant with a mix of different music. We sat in the corner at the bar and got more privacy to ourselves. It was a little awkward at times when our waiter leaned over the side of the wall to talk to us or give us different glasses for tasting.

Service - 4/5 - Waiters were friendly, attentive and gave us insight on each beverage we got. They asked about dietary restrictions and allergies before the start. Our waiter did not specify how many omakase tastings we were to have with each drink (6 drinks overall and about 14-15 omakase tasting). It was unclear so me and my girlfriend kind of guessed on how much to drink or just ended up chugging (which we had no problem with haha).  Overall, more clarity would've been helpful so we could've paced ourselves.

Beverage Tasting - 5/5 - The tasting came with 2 full glasses of wine and 4 full shots of sake (big pours). If you're wondering if this is worth it, IT IS!! This made a huge difference in the overall experience. The 2 glasses of wine were not sweet (how I like it) and more on the earthy/crisp end. It paired well with many of the tastings. The premium sake was nothing short of AMAZING. The sake completely elevated the omakase tastings to another level. All four of them were smooth, crisp and on the drier end. Sadly we do not remember the names of the sake/wines (we were pretty buzzed). We firmly believe the omakase would not have been as spectacular without the beverage tasting.

Omakase Tasting - 5/5 - I don't know where to begin with this. All the fish was extremely fresh and flavorful. My personal favorite was the caviar and tuna dish with bread. The uni was spectacular along with the variation of tuna, yellowtail and salmon. There were even some fish that we don't typically eat (mackerel) that we tried for the first time. It did not disappoint! Since it was my birthday, they brought dessert with a candle and a card from the staff. The ice cream was amazing. My girlfriend still craves it till this day! Overall 5/5!!

If you're thinking of having a solid meal and splurging for an occasion, this is the PERFECT spot. It will not disappoint. Our overall bill was $923 with tax and tip. It will be an occasion we will remember forever.

Three out of four of us had diarrhea after dinner in Shuko. We have tried to reach out afterwards, and front office said GM will come back. However it has been 3 weeks and Shuko GM did not come back to us - not even a sorry! Really really disappointed and upset with this restaurant. Not going back any point in our life. It is not just about food but also about integrity and customer service.

First time back at Shuko post pandemic and it's gone downhill. Restaurant felt dingy and the floors were not clean. Our server greeted us in an aggressive way insisting we open the drink portion of the menu while she stood watching over our shoulder. But the real issue was watching a bar full of sushi chefs pre-slicing the fish!!! This is a $230 meal before gratuity, drinks and tax. Pre cutting the fish is unacceptable! Sushi is meant to be cut to order as fish starts degrading in quality from that point. Watching the chefs pile up stacks of precut fish was shocking. We ended up deciding to leave and the manager was very rude about it. She tried to lecture me as to how Shuko is a fine dining Omakase and that everything is made to order. She clearly does not have experience with high end sushi outside of her stint as Shuko. Save your money. There are better experiences in the city for that kind of money.

The dining experience at Shuko was good customer service is horrible. My card was charged double, and the manager, Mary Luu treated me like her biggest inconvenience of the day when I asked for a refund on my card. Expected sincere apologies for the honest mistake but it must be the most impossible task for this management.

Fantastic sushi at Shuko. There are high expectations when one walks through that unmarked door, but rest assured because every dish is executed very well. Started off with a milk bread, toro, caviar, and uni appetizer. Then came toro that was very soft and just melted in one's mouth. It was a good indicator of the quality of the nigiri that would be coming. The Hokkaido uni was one of the best I've ever had from that region. I also enjoyed the Japanese sea perch which I believe the chef referred to as akamutsu, though I've heard it called nodoguro at other places. Spanish mackerel was good, and even the horse mackerel (which I'm not usually that big of a fan of) was okay here. Scallop, soft shrimp, hirame, amberjack and others were all great. Some pieces are blow torched, some have little dollops of sauce added on top (yuzu pepper, for example). The meal ended with a soy ice cream that we all liked. No apple pie though.

Our server Lua was very nice and knowledgeable. We appreciated her suggesting to us to not order the add-ons right at the beginning, but to wait a little bit to determine if we'll need them. It turned out that we were quite full with the standard set, and did not need the add-ons. We did order some Pappy Van Winkle 10-year and 12-year bourbons to finish off the meal. The restaurant carries a nice array of Japanese whiskies, American bourbons (I saw a lot of Michter's), and sakes. 

They called me to confirm my reservation twice - once on the day before (which I called back and spoke to someone) and then again on the day of (which when i called back got no response). This is confusing, as it made me wonder if my first confirm never went through. It made me question how effectively the service staff were communicating with each other. We were not able to get a corner section of the bar (which would've been nice as we were a party of three), but that's fine, others booked it first. Aside from those two minor things, everything else was terrific.

I thought Shuko was as good as Ginza Onodera is food-wise, though the latter has a more impressive interior and higher price tag. This is a more intimate setting, similar to that of Kura.

Typical omakase experience. The place is a bit on the less of a zen experience and more of a bustling and loud experience. Still, the food is well presented and the sushi is good but not memorable. I remember this place having too much going on in the peripheral, making it harder to focus in the sushi.

If you're looking for a perfectly executed omakase experience, look no further than Shuko.

The vibes here are hip. It's a minimalist Japanese design on the inside with hip hop playing at a perfect volume in the background. It's a mix of traditional with classic NY street style.

The food was unbelievable. It was probably the only omakase experience I've had where I actually left feeling full. Every single bite was delicious. Stand outs were everything uni, tuna, and a sea trout I'll never forget. 

Make your reservation early, get the uni tasting, be emotionally prepared for an unforgettable meal! Oh, and make sure to sit at the counter!

The best Omakase in NY - On this special day, I enjoy the heartbeat on the tip of my tongue.  So beautiful environment.  The quality of fish is amazing . The highlights tonight is  uni toro caviar toasted , so amazing. My  chef tonight was Jacky, he did wonderful job of explaining each of  the dish and answering all of  my questions. He was very professional. The service is very good.  I hope I can  go back in the near future.

Prior to our dinner we only heard great reviews about dining at Shuko so our expectations were high. I can easily say our expectations were beyond met. From the first course to the dessert every dish was INCREDIBLE. Each piece of sushi was an experience of its own. I've never had better uni and now I crave it every day. The service at Shuko was amazing as well. From our knowledgeable sushi chef to our waitress and the sommelier. All were great!
Wow one of the best omakase experiences ever.  Your senses will be delighted.  Everyone is so friendly too!  Please enjoy!
One of the best Omakase experiences of my life. The uni tasting with sake pairing was unparalleled and the highlight of the night.

Good place nice atmosphere but worst omakase meal ever!!!! everything is so wrong when you bring a family here (over4 people)
1. If the host would let us know before we made a reservation that sushi bar only available if you're party of 4 or less than 4 but if more than 4 people technically they seat you at a table in Omakase restaurant which is weird!
2. Services is average for Michelin guide restaurant but i expect a better service compared to price you pay 
3. Every fish tasted fresh but look sad, since my group get to sat down at the table so this place decided to place your "Omakase" fish course on a huge plate. They provide you with 15pcs they divided by 3 on each plate.
Every plate look so dead.
4. Rice doesn't have any taste and still uncooked
5. They served 3 sushi roll for your "omakase" meal 
6. Tricky tricky this place serve soy sauce for your "omakase" meal 
7. Wagyu sushi: cold! I don't how long it's been sit there ughh!!

 
I know this place from Youtube since their owners shows their good ingredients but what they are right now is completely different. We're from LA, we've had a lot of omakase restaurants but never experience anything like this place before. 

Maybe i set my expectations too high for this place. Overall if you love sushi don't come to this place it will ruin your night.

One day I offhandedly told my boyfriend I was craving sushi. Within an hour he told me he made a omakase reservation for later that night. OMAKASE?! Sheesh. FOLKS, NEVER SETTLE. 

Anyways, to the omakase. What a wonderful, DELICIOUS, and filling experience. We were seated at the bar, where we got an exciting view of the sushi chefs' technique. The appetizers included this tart, refreshing seaweed dish and a toasted milk bread with toro tartare and caviar dish. Both were so flavorful! I could've eaten more of both. The rest of the evening included delicious selections, one after the other. There was a spicy sushi with Thai chilis that I sadly did not catch the exact name of, but will remember forever. 

So that said, my only suggestion would be to offer patrons some sort of paper menu, as I repeatedly couldn't catch what the waitress / the sushi chef announced when they placed the next selection in front of us. I would've loved to have a record.

This restaurant is easy to miss as there's no sign and only a door marked with flowers to go by.  Beyond the door is a sleek space with an intimate sushi bar, a handful of smaller tables, and a private room tucked away downstairs.  The omakase features their famous tuna tartare caviar served with toast and a luxe assortment of nice thick cuts that are also typically served at other top sushi bars in the city.  As such, I wouldn't say the omakase is that memorable if you have had the experience before.  It's solid and enjoyable.  What blew me away (and contributed to the 5 star review) was the tasting of uni from Hokkaido, Santa Barbara and Maine paired with sake.  I've never come across that on a menu before and it was a truly unique culinary experience.  I'm thankful to our server who steered us in the right direction as we almost opted for the uni supplement on the toast instead.     Go to Shuko for a fun night to splurge and enjoy life!

Insider's Tip: Book the sushi bar and request the corner on the shorter side - best seats in the house.

Phenomenal omakase experience. The restaurant is sleek and intimate with tons of sushi bar seating so you're up close and personal with that sushi. The quality of the fish is amazing with generous cuts.

The uni add on to the toast was worth the extra $50 as it added a richness to it. Some of the favorites were salmon, toro, mackerel, and the torched items. The dessert was even really good as I believe it was a soy sauce ice cream of some sort. Was a great treat and didn't have too much umami flavor despite what it was. We asked for a sake recommendation from the waiter based on our liking of junmai gingo and they picked one that was light and refreshing.
Fantastic food and service! Nice spot for a special occasion. Favorites were the toro and the wagyu

We came to this place for celebrating our friend birthday but very disappointed.

First, we booked for party of 5 people. We expect that omakase would seat us at the bar but NOT!!!  They brought us to the private room in the basement that very dark and small. We felt uncomfortable to sat there. They said we have to called them first if we want to sit at the bar and we won't sit next to each other. I think they have to inform us that party for 5 will only seat at the table and we won't be able to seat at the bar because of maximum is for 4 bla bla bla but the didn't. 

We're deal with the hostess for at least 10 mins about changing the table. They offer us to reschedule and come back at 9pm but if we didn't want this room or rebooked the time schedule. We will get charged for cancellation about $70 per person. What was happening to us!!! We showed up on time, no notice or any informed that we won't get the bar or that room. This was ridiculous. They forced us to sat there even we didn't feel comfortable. We didn't want to pay for the fee if we walked out. so, we sat there unhappy.

10mins later one of their severs came back to check on us. And we were hopeless and wanted to leave we asked her to check again at least for the table and Thank God! We got the new table upstairs that much better!!! So, were like okay let gave them a chance. 

We ordered one bottle sake and yes 5 omakases. First one looked like tuna salad. Second, was fatty tuna caviar on top with Japanese bread. This one was good and we looking forward to have sushi. Their sushi was fresh but looked so simple and normal. We paid $228 each so, we expected to see nice presentation on the fish and more fancy but they're all just plain fish like seriously plain fishes!!!!! 

Server told us what kind of fish that we had. She told us the same fish twice. Seriously? I told them that we got the same fish but she refused and said that was a mistake. And also What kind of omakase gave us a cut roll? Is that normal?  Is it supposed to be hand roll?
WHATEVER!!!
We tried to gave them a second chance but Failed!!! 


We won't be back here. Wasted of money. Very disappointed.
Not recommended!!!!

I really enjoyed Shuko.. very chill and laidback environment. The omakase is clean and tasty. Love the real hip hop soundtrack playing in the background. Def NYC vibe with Japanese twist. Loved it and thank you!
We didn't get the apple pie but we got ice cream and it was so good! Wondering how this ice cream and their apple pie together must have been

My goodness. What a fun night out. The place ain't cheap but I try not to eat sushi often but when I do I go for the highest quality and experience. Shuko did not disappoint. Amazing Som. Decadent food. Great memories.

Shuko had a great omakase menu with carefully crafted pieces and talented sushi chefs. 

While the price tag is quite high for the experience, the 16 piece with toro and caviar, crab and cucumber dish was delicious. 

The only thing I wasn't that impressed with was the dining experience. Maybe it was them playing Drake and Kanye. Maybe it was because I felt so cramped sitting in their space. It just didn't have a comfortable environment.
Ok sushi and shari.  Instead oh edomae style this place is more arranged. Overall nothing outstanding and I will not go back again.

Badly organized sushi Omakase.  Each piece were good but not omakase level. And servers were so badly educated. Main chef was nice but his team were not at his level at all some sashimi his team made prepared had scale left on. Over all it is not worth of the price.

OMG. This meal was amazing! Very attentive service, as well as a good amount of food (two apps, 16 pieces of sushi, palette cleanser, then a really nice dessert with a generous glass of aged sake. 

They have a great sake selection, organized by region of Japan and at all price points. They also have an extensive wine menu too, both by the glass and bottle.

Will definitely return!

Amazing and very fresh sushi! I loved the intimate counter experience and courses were served quickly with little fuss. The omakase is a huge meal so go hungry! Towards the end I started to get very full and without even having to ask, the chef accommodated my appetite by reducing the rice portion so I could eat more of the fish. In addition, Shuko has many reasonably priced sake options to pair with your meal.

The most fantastic omakase experience I've ever had. The cuts kept building on eat other and progressively got better and better. Snapper, Squid with Lime Zest, Wagyu Uni, Charcoal Seared Toro, Ebi, all had so much depth and were bites I'm going to think about for a long time. Soy ice cream at the end was a perfect cap.

Only fault would maybe be the apps, the tuna caviar on toast was a bit of a letdown, butteriness on the bread overpowered the toro & caviar and it was a otherwise better eating it with the spoon on its own

Otherwise our waiter Felix was highly attentive and super friendly, excited to try them again at some point.

Let me preface this review by saying this was the first Omakase experience most our group have experienced.

When you first make your way to Shuko, you will be forgiven for walking past it before realizing you did. There is no obvious sign, besides some wood paneling and a non descript black door. You pull it open and walk in, immediately taken away from the streets of NYC and into the world of Chefs Jimmy Lau and Nick Kim.

Inside you will find a sushi counter with plenty of seating with reservations up to 4 people. If you're like us with a party of 6, you are led down somewhat steep staircase flanked by black stone and shown to a small private dining room which looks like it was carved out of natural stone. Moderately intimate and away from the bustle of the busy Sushi counter.

The  only option on the menu right now is Omakase. Which consisted of  2 appetizer courses, 16 pieces of nigiri, and a dessert course. Each seat is set with chopsticks, and glass which is immediately filled with chilled water. We are offered to scan a QR code to browse the 20 page drink menu, or to use the provided tablet. Only 2 signature cocktails on the menu, otherwise a full bar is available and can accommodate almost any cocktail request. The list of sake and wine is extensive and offers plenty of options that will make your wallet feel much lighter at the end of evening. 

It doesn't take long for drinks to arrive, glasses are provided for each diner when sake is ordered, all served chilled and placed back in ice to stay cold. 

It's not long before the first appetizer course comes out. Dungeoness crab with cucumber, scallion, and nori. A small but flavor packed first course with mild tastes of the ocean between the crab and hydrated nori. The second appetizer course comes out, Toro with black caviar, served with milk toast. The recommendation is to take all of the toro and caviar and spread across the provided toast. This one definitely tastes like the sea, but well balanced. The milk bread doing the heavy lifting for this dish, preventing the flavors from being overpowering. 

Now with the appetizers done, we all await the 16 pieces of nigiri with excitement. During that time we are served soy sauce, pickled ginger, and folded cleansing cloth. Do not do what one of us did and use it to clean your whole hand. This is folded in a way to clean your fingers between each piece of nigiri, as we are recommended to eat with our fingers. Soy sauce is optional, but all nigiri comes dressed by the chefs. If you are going to dip, we are instructed to dip with the fish not the rice. 

Over the next hour or so, we are served 16 different pieces of nigiri. Saba with myago, Hotate with shiso dressing, seared Wagyu with Uni, the most delicate Ebi These were the standouts from 16 pieces. The Akami was also delightful. I'm usually not a fan, but I guess when you are being served the best quality fish from Japan, its not surprising. The final piece wasn't fish, but a palette cleanser. A fresh way to end the meal. At the end we are offered the option to indulge any of the served pieces again, a la carte if desired. Some of us indulged, others satisfied. 

Dessert is ice cream that is served with a candle for me since it's a birthday celebration, even if it is a week early. It's ice cream made from Soba, yes that Soba. It was delicious and unique. All of us were very surprised by how good it was. 

Overall probably one of the best meals I have ever had. I will probably be thinking of that seared Wagyu with Uni for a very long time, that Saba with Myago really set a high bar at the beginning and will also be on my mind for a long time. One of us are correct to point out how perfect the rice was. Not overcooked, not too dry and the perfect portion. It's true that the rice might be the most import part of nigiri, and can make or break even the best piece of fish. The service was impeccable and we never felt forgotten or like we were a burden. All of our questions answered to give us an experience we won't soon forget. 

As most fine dining experiences, we were left wanting more. Some of us because there was still room, other because we simply didnt want the night to end. 

The bill is brought while drinks are being finished. The check is paid, and we are led back up the stairs. Walking past the still busy Sushi counter as the chefs continue to serve little piece of heaven. A symphony of simple, but quality ingredients made by hands that truly care. 

We walk back through the black non descript door and leave the world of Chef Jimmy Lau and Nick Kim and are back on the streets of NYC. We spent a little over 2 hours in their world, and what a trip it was.

Shuko is so awesome, I wish I could hang here every day. It's the little things that make Shuko so awesome. Hokkaido Uni was really great, I wanted to order every thing off their menu, but glad that I chose Hokkaido Uni. Team is super courteous and will help you with everything. It's awesome.

This restaurant has clearly gone down hill. I went when they opened a few years ago and the food was truly sublime. I went again last night, and I have to say I am extremely disappointed. The food is now average at best. The service is very good, the food just does not live up to expectations, or what the previously produced. I wouldn't rate this as an avoid at all costs situation, but I would exhaust all your other options first. The strangest thing to me is not having a single piece of salmon in their omakase. With the Omaksae, only one of the nine pieces was memorable and the rest were forgettable. It's sad to see how far downhill Shuko has gone.

Wanted to give this place a chance as I am a huge fan of Omakase and have been to most of the top omakase restaurants in the city.  Food was ok but definitely not worth the steamy price coupled with the poor service.  Also the 'outdoor' setting was more like an abandoned alley way with scattered tables and poor lighting.  Plenty of better options out there folks!

Probably 3rd Shuko experience.  For ~$350 of sushi, was the worst delivery sushi we've had in the city.  Sparse servings, a little overdone with embellishments to hide small fish portions, and overall limited quality to the sushi grade fish.  Will not go back.  To be clear, would have been pleased with the experience for like $80 but there are some clear disconnects!  Not sure what shuko is going for here.

This meal was insanely expensive!! I didn't find the sushi to be too exciting or luxurious for the price point.  If the atmosphere had been a little more ambient maybe I wouldn't mind paying so much!  The staff was as frigid as the outdoor dining space.  Sitting on metal chairs froze my butt off and they have one teeny tiny electric heater in an open air space to be shared among two giant tables.  The only nice person was a gentleman with a beard who brought us more green tea.  I went inside to use the restroom and said hi to the chefs and I was ignored, I don't think anyone is happy here.  Sigh, it was a special occasion but we all left dinner feeling kinda sad.

The staff is super friendly and knowledgeable. 

The kitchen had gluten free soy sauce which was a big plus. The ambiance and outside setting is adorable!

For appetizers we ordered the brussel sprouts, topped with Bonito flakes (which was amazing) and the ceviche which was quite bland. 

The entree prices are a bit exorbitant. We had a set for 2 people which included 1 small roll and 7 pieces of nigiri per person for $163 and 1 spicy Toro roll for $29.

Overall, the fish was good but not great, rather bland except for for spicy trout roll which was seasoned nicely.

Wow amazing! 

Beautiful and safe environment for omakase. My first experience since covid and this place has done a wonderful job. And top it off the chef came out to serve us and check in on house. 


My first time here and it will not be my last.
*** get the spicy lobster   it was amazing***

Fyi the have a extensive whiskey collection!
Ask the staff for recommendations

Remarkably bad service. I placed a sizeable online order for pick up directly thru Shuko's website and drove in from Brooklyn in pouring rain, only to find the restaurant closed. Multiple phone calls, emails, and online messages were never returned. After two days of calls I finally get in touch with someone who isn't really helpful. I'm told to monitor my CC for a refund and call back again in a few days  if there are any issues. This is no way to run a supposedly high end establishment.

My husband and I came here the night before a vacation a few months ago and we had a lovely time sitting at the counter.  We were able to get a reservation a couple weeks out, but when we arrived we had to wait a little bit for our table - they took us downstairs where we had a drink while we waited. It was a little annoying to have to wait, but the whiskey cocktails we ordered were delicious 

The service was impeccable and the food was excellent.  The reason for not 5 stars is that I think there are other sushi restaurants that are at a lower price point that are just as good and in some respects better.  That being said, I think this restaurant is worth a visit to try for yourself.  

I took some pictures, which you can see for yourself, but here are some of the dishes I remember (and I should note that they were able to make gluten free alternatives for my husband) 
Toro caviar with the side of milk bread
The trout had very nice Thai curry flavors
Duck was very tasty, but the smaller piece was a tad overcooked for me
I remember liking almost all of the sushi pieces
In particular, the toro sushi piece was delicious - they started with the toro sushi here in the sequence, which was interesting
We added a few pieces at the end since we were still hungry and these were all incredible, I unfortunately don't know exactly what they were because we told the chef to surprise us

Overall, we had a wonderful experience and I think it's worth coming to experience

This is such a fun spot and totally the sort of place that makes you feel happy to live in NYC.
That said, I didn't eat a single piece of sushi that I'm still thinking about and I am totally a person who thinks about sushi. Some of the rice was hard.
Also, they no longer offer a just sushi omakase and a Kaiseke menu. Just Kaiseke and it's a little more food than I wanted and then it costs extra to include premium sushi-- like toro and uni, which seems a bit lame.
So, three stars for now.
You won't find a better atmosphere or food under one roof. Jimmy lau is a genius!!!!!!

Exceptional small dishes and impeccable customer service. I felt like I was having a dinner party with friends. From the hostess to the waiters to the bartenders, everyone was so kind and positive. Our sushi chef was super friendly too! Come for the food, stay for the service. Be nice to the staff! They might give you multiple glasses of free sake and then end the night with a group tequila shot. ‍
Really good but really expensive. With tip we spent almost $500 pp. def hit it up for a special occasion! Each bite was terrific. Fish was incredibly high quality.

Hidden gem. This is not in the rotation of omakase restaurants you hear people talking about in nyc. But it should be. Omakase only restaurant that serves you about 4 small dishes followed by 15 pieces of nigiri and dessert. The sushi set that is served is simple and amazing. It is as simple as toro brushed with soy sauce. But it is perfection. I considered myself an uni queen and I have to say... Shuko served me the best piece of uni I have ever had in my life. The ambiance was great. Intimate restaurant style. Chef Ry was great. Next time I will make sure I come for a special occasion, very expensive restaurant, but worth it for something special.

Went to Shuko Saturday night and would rate the place 4.5 stars. Even with our reservation, we had to wait a little downstairs by the bathroom. The staff were nice and served us drinks while we were waiting. The drink prices were around $20, so expect to pay a bit on top of your order.

Once we were seated to the sushi bar, there were two options for omakase which were sushi omakase ($180) and there was a sushi omakase + kaiseki ($225).  For an omakase, it is fairly expensive, but the quality of the sushi was amazing. Eating each piece was an experience on it's own, but i wish there was some kind of conversation between the sushi chief and my friends. Serving staff and the food was great, but the Sushi chiefs were in their own world and just making each dish quickly as they can. It makes sense because they would need to continuously serve a handful of people at once, but wish it was a bit on a slower pace behind the  counter. 

I could continue on, but it would be a repeat with other 4+ star reviews. My overall experience in Shuko was pleasant, but too sure what other reviewers with 3 stars and below are talking about. Given the quality of the food and fish, you're paying for the experience and quality. If you want to go somewhere with premium fish and service, just go to Japan. But for New York, I would go back to Shuko for special occasions and would recommend this establishment to my peers.

This place is OVERPRICED AND UNPROFESSIONAL. The chef talks too much in front of the food, it's never happened in any other Michelin restaurant before. The sushi chef never talk too much while making the sushi. Other staffs are roaming around the counter but literally didn't do anything but starring at clients. They offered overpriced omakase and kaiseki, meaning nothing marvelous but ordinary. We've spent $500 for nothing. They really need to consider upgrade the menu in order to match the price.

First time omakase, and boy was this a treat! The sushi just melts away in your mouth like butter..they give the sushi in timed intervals but not long enough where you get hungry waiting. Flavors were bright and vibrant with every bite. Will be back

Not worth the price - while the food is great and space is beautiful, the service did not live up to the amount you spend to be there.  If I'm paying hundreds of dollars for two people to have a nice meal, every part of the experience should be held to a certain standard. Been to other omakases where you can pay much less while feeling like you are a valued customer instead  of another person coming through the door.

The ambiance here is uniquely hip - 90s/early 2000s hip hop classics bump through the speakers while the sushi chefs at the bar don Yankee hats instead of the traditional white toque. It makes this omakase/kaiseki experience uniquely New York - diners here range from foodies to finance bros to "impress your date" couples, you're coming here to spend money and everyone's OK with it.
My friends and I went for the kaiseki selection, because, why not... and really enjoyed the prepped dishes that came with the selection. Highlights include a crab dish that looked almost like a coleslaw until you realize that what looked like shredded cabbage was luxurious sweet crab meat. There was also the tuna tartare with caviar on top served with a slice of milk bread... it was fun to make your own little bites. The beef cheek was also insanely fall apart and tender.
The sushi part of the kaiseki (the standard omakase course) was really good as well... though I suppose I find it hard to say if anything really distinguished itself from any of the other omakases I've had. It's not that the fish wasnt good... it was really nicely done, but there wasn't a ton of differentiation. I think I'm only mentioning this because I would recommend that if you dine here, you should go for the kaiseki to have something unique to Shuko vs any other well respected restaurant.
Service was really nice and seamless - as we were having a really good conversational flow going, things just kinda came and left the table without us noticing. I appreciated that very much. 
The hostess was very considerate and reminded us discreetly that we shouldn't use flash at the table - standard practice for me, but for other diners I think that's a nice heads up so that they're not reprimanded mid-meal.

It is definitely overpriced, the omakase quality doesn't meet with the price at all. It costs me $240 but I think I can get way better experience in ex. Sushi Yusuda or even Tanoshi Sushi bar with much lower price. The finish or seafood itself is okay, but the rice is so sticky, sometimes even raw. Also the ginger they provide is way too smoky. Won't come here again.

This is not an omakase to write home about. In fact, I was expecting "the most esthetically pleasing omakase" and it was not that. No gold flakes, no caviar. The piece you see in pics is a $28 supplement. How would I know to order that? omakase is where the chef is supposed to point you in right direction. Overall most of the pieces were on the safe side, and I was expecting culinary adventure.

For the price point, it is extremely disappointing. I think most pieces were actually pretty firm for what I'm used to in best omakase and most didn't even taste cured. The lotus root palate cleanser was too intense at the end. I have had $65 omakase in SF better than what I had here for over $600 for two people with drinks. I was surprised when we started off with toro. There was a few good pieces but it really seemed to go downhill rather than expected upward progression. Also it was my best friend's first time trying omakase; I specifically asked for wagyu in special requests and just to be sure, asked for the $70 add on despite the fact that the price should make anyone gasp. What was truly shocking though was fact that despite all that, we never had wagyu the entire evening. Such a disappointment NYC...
Great ambience, high quality service and exceptionally fresh fish. Loved the understated but original flavor combinations in the kaiseki menu.

The front door is pretty discreet. So discreet, I walked by it and didn't realize it! Just how I love most of my restaurants in NYC. Unmarked & understated, very on trend. We went all out and did the kaiseki. We started off with cooked food and ended the meal with sushi. I loved more of the dishes than I disliked, so overall, it was a beautiful meal coupled with great friends to match the 3 hour, ever so subtle and cozy meal. Be prepared to go a culinary journey of your favorite foods in tiny bite form. The highlight of the meal was definitely the sushi... though I found it odd that they ended the meal with a basic tuna roll. I would have kept it sushi only, and start from mellow to richness, but they seem to do things a bit . backwards here. I don't need excess & unnecessary stuff! By the time dessert hit (granita & apple pie), I was pretty stuffed.

3.5 star.  I was not blown away by the food or service. For 500+ for two, I was expecting a bit more.

1. The female waitress who served app to us spoke in such a quick manner,  I couldn't make out what the dish was half of time.
2. The main sushi chef was very professional, but the other chefs were young and were not acting as they were working at a top notch restaurant.  Don't get me wrong,  I don't mind young chefs.  In fact, one of the best meals I had was served by a young chef who was exceptionally talented.  The young chefs at Shuko were joking around with each other.  One of the guests who came in was probably an acquaintance of one of the chefs.  They interacted a lot while the chef was not that interactive with the other patrons.
3. The restaurant was trying to create a casual and hip ambience.  I liked the decor, and appreciated the music selection, but if you are used to the more reserved sushi restaurant ambience,  this is not the right choice of restaurant for you.
4. Out of the all the sushi restaurants I have been to, this is the only one that served toro in the very beginning, contrary to many traditional sushi restaurants.  If you like the traditional progression, light to fatty, again, I recommend skipping this restaurant. 
5. There was one highlight during the meal.  The main chef served us a muscle piece from an orange clam.  The piece had a flaky and crunchy texture which I enjoyed a lot.
6. My husband was looking forward to the apple tart with ice cream as dessert which was served previously.  Instead of that, they served strawberry sorbet, which was disappointing. 
7. There was a home made pickled sushi piece that was served towards the very end to cleanse the pallet.  I guess the intention was to finish the meal with a clean taste.  In my opinion, it was better to serve it on the beginning to whet the appetite.
Hard to find and discreetly hidden away, this place is a gem. Fantastic service, excellent fish and an overall delightful meal. I would come back.
I don't know why they're so expensive. Vibe was good but the food/ sushi was not as great as the price. I went more than 20 sushi restaurants in Manhattan. I'll never come back here.

It's definitely good sushi, but for the price you can do better in nyc. I loved Neta when these guys were there, but at a lower price point. The fish here is fresh and well cut, but it lacks some of the "wow" courses you usually get at $200+. The cooked courses, which some say are the best part were pretty good, but not fantastic.

Shuko is very high end and very pricey. It was a really wonderful romantic date experience but way overpriced for what you get. It's 180 per person for the tasting menu and 100 for the Sake. There is also an extended 225 per person menus. There is a chef per every 4 people there. Service is out of this world and very attentive. Our favorite dish was the fatty tuna hand roll. I can't say I'll go back here, it is more of a one and done kind of experience but overall really great. Make sure you make a reservation ahead of time and cancel if you can't attend as it's a 180 per person cancellation fee. Enjoy!

Really enjoyed my experience at Shuko, sat at the bar and had the Kaiseki omakase paired with a few drinks. Our sushi chef was friendly and I enjoyed trying all the various small Japanese dishes and of course the fresh nigiri. It's upscale dining, so the price, quality, and service is expected - I certainly enjoyed my time and will definitely come back again!

If you have a special occasion, come here.

Came here to Shuko Saturday Evening with my partner to celebrate our Anniversary. We made a reservation for 5:30pm at the Sushi Bar (recommended) and was seated immediately. From the outside, the unmarked door was reminiscent of a speakeasy with an air of exclusivity. The ambiance and decor was 5/5 with high ceilings, smooth hardwood bar surface and great modern music. 

From the moment we walked in, the service was impeccable from the waitress helping you push the chair in to the water being consistently refilled. The highlight of our night was our sushi chef Jeff located on the south side of sushi bar; he truly made our experience special, sharing his expertise on the art of sushi making and thoughts on the fish. The waitstaff also learned of our anniversary and comped us a free apple pie dessert!

We opted for the Omakase for $180/person which was the perfect amount of food. Shuko nigiri's are not the most traditional with unique "toppings" such as yuzu or ginger etc on top of each piece. Personally i thought "topping" accentuated the flavor while distracted depending on the piece. Rice and soy sauce was very memerable. Would rate the food a 4.5/5.0.

Pros: Best service and atmosphere among omakase restaurants in New York. The grilled toro and uni pieces were amazing. Housemade ginger and soy sauce.
Considerations: This is not your traditional omakase, the pieces taste unique and original.

So many reviewers consider Shuko the best Sushi Omikase experience in NYC. Nothing could be further from the truth. It was ok, but overpriced. The service was excellent, but the sushi was average.

The place was packed with supposedly knowledgable sushi lovers. When I think that you can have a fantastic Sushi Omikase experience only 8 blocks away at Sugarfish at 1/3 to 1/4 the price, I wonder what some of these so called "experts" are thinking. Ok--the ambiance is a little nicer....but so what!!!

I can see why this is four stars. The food and atmosphere is superb. But for $180 without tax or tip the service is really not good. The servers bark out what they are serving with little explanation of origin etc. the wine pouring was very uneven. I preferred other omakase that is more affordable. That said certain elements were very nice like the excellent nori (always crisp).

The sushi omakase ($180 per person) was okay. Room temperature sushi was fresh and for $180, there was a bit more additional pieces than your regular $120-$150 omakases. All of the sushi was a bit on the "too salty" palette for me and the loud music and choice of music just didn't create the vibe for me. I get that it's a "hip" "new" place(?) but  I didn't leave the place thinking, "oh yeah, I'm coming back here." A "meh" for $180 for me.

Torn between 4 and 5. We had 9pm reservations on a Saturday and luckily was able to come around 8:30. The restaurant is narrow and packed until we left (after midnight). The wood bar is stunning - you can tell the chef takes care of it. There are three tables you can be seated in but I wouldn't come to Shuko to be away from the action. Sit at the bar. 

There are two options for the menu - sushi omakase ($180) and the sushi omakase + kaiseki. You can choose a few additional items, including an A5 wagyu dish ($70). We ordered the omakase and kaiseki choice ($225), a few additional items, a bottle of sake for me ($58), and a kaiseki beverage pairing ($175) for my partner. 

You start off with the kaiseki menu. There are around 6 or 7 dishes that come out. Highlights were a fashion broth at the end, uni caviar toro on milk bread, and the octopus. The milk bread was prepared so soft and perfect for the uni, caviar and toro. We ordered the A5 wagyu which was delicious however, I've had better prepared A5 wagyu in New York. You can't fault the buttery-ness of it but it was just a touch over cooked. 

Omakase - all around delicious. They're not as generous with their fish cuts as tanoshi or nakazawa but they have a few unique items. It's an 17 piece omakase and the later half of the omakase gets better. They did a toro with bird eye Chile's that was very spicy and delicious. My favorite piece was the fried oyster with black truffle on top. Melts in your mouth. The rice was good, but a little tough. 

Why not a 5 star? 
The biggest reason is because they kept forgetting our beverage pairing. The pairing should align with certain pieces in a timely manner but because there was a delay, it affected the pairing. And the pairing isn't cheap. The meal was just under a grand for the two of us and if we're spending that kind of money on dinner, then make sure the servers are attentive enough to pair the meal and drinks in a punctual manner. 

The other reason is because although it was a delicious meal, I've had a handful of better omakase for the same or lower price in ny. It's a pet peeve when the fish cut is stingy and if the rice isn't perfect in texture, flavor and temperature.

TL;DR do not waste your time or money. We flew here for my wife's birthday. One of the top hotels in NYC, first class flight, and what I thought was going to be a great dinner planned months in advance. I want you to understand I wanted to love this restaurant and to convince my wife and myself that this place was great. This was unfortunately the worst sushi experience we've ever had.  The receptionist was completely rude and pretentious and hung up on me when I asked about how to find the restaurant. Once we eventually found the restaurant and glared at the then sheepish receptionist, we were greeted by a rather friendly waiter. He was actually fantastic and I was very hopeful that the rest of the night would be wonderful. However, the sushi was unbearably bland and sinewy. Additionally, the presentation was noticeably gimmicky. Almost as if they were pandering to non-asian viewers of sushi documentaries who are told that real sushi connoisseurs eat with their hands. Avoid, don't pass go, collect your money and go elsewhere.

I stopped in for a solo dinner while traveling on business. I decided to go for the full (larger) chefs tasting. They do have tasting pairings which include wine and sake. The food itself was great. I went in hungry and the larger tasting was definitely enough food, although the servers do seem to push the supplemental sushi options. The presentation and freshness was on point and I had the opportunity to try several new types of sushi which I hadn't had before, much less seen on menus before at other places. One of the strangest things I was presented was tempuraed cod sperm - eek! This one I tried and can't say I finish. I also had needlefish and trout (which were both new to me). Overall the experience was great, but the price tag was steep. I'd defiantly come back and recommend to anyone looking for a special occasion dinner or just something new to try for a bit of adventure.

I came here on a Thursday night with 2 friends, sat at the bar and had the $180 omakase option.  This was one of my friend's first time doing omakase and shuko did not disappoint.  I have also been to sushi nakazawa before. If I have to describe shuko, it is casual and modern.  They have their own touch of style.  They had on some hip hop music, so it was a fun vibe.  As for the sushi, it was delicious and we did not want it to end.  It definitely felt different from sushi nakazawa. Shuko puts its own twist into the style compared the to the traditional.  I definitely would love to come back!

Shuko was incredibly amazing. All the sushi was on point. It is $180 per person, so it is probably not the spot to have a casual dinner date. Save it for special occasions. It is definitely worth it to check it out at least once.

Came here again. A good friend treated me for my birthday and we did the sushi omakase but added the uni/caviar/toro supplement. The restaurant surprised us with a delicious birthday dessert (apple pie and soba ice cream, which was amazing) and card. Service was great. My tea was constantly refilled and all of the food was delicious. My favorite piece by far was surprisingly the fried cod topped with black truffle (see photos). Would return just for this! I highly recommend.
Great place for omakase sushi. They have two choices for it. You can also have the sake pairing with the omakase as well. Waitstaff was super attentive and very nice.

One of the best omakase experiences we've had! Loved the bumping soundtrack (90s hip hop!), and I couldn't stop rubbing the ash bar. 

We chose the kaiseki menu, and a bottle of sake. Husband explained that he liked the crispness of Sauvignon blanc, so the sommelier paired us up beautifully with a crisp fruit forward sake. 

The service was playful and fun, the servers joking around with us as they placed beautiful dishes of poached lobster, fresh scallops, and duck in front of us. They served us a perfectly clear bowl of dashi consommé that my husband was OBSESSED with! He was like - why don't more sushi places serve this as their soup??

Honestly the next time we go we may just stick to the sushi only omakase- as the omakase was the BEST part of our experience! We had a chef all to ourselves who explained the origins of the fish (we learned that trout is super similar to salmon! Who knew?) and placed perfect mouthfuls in front of us. He was mindful of my husband's aversion to uni (which I think is insane since I can eat uni for every meal)! 

Our meal ended with their signature apple pie which was an awesome ending. 

Standing ovation y'all - Shuko was such an enjoyable experience from beginning to end! And that ash bar!!! That's what LUXURY feels like!

The omakase included very basic fish, we usually expect an omakase to have exotic fish but we were disappointed with the usual types of fish, some of which were chewy, hard in some areas, while other pieces were multiple cuts of fish put together (scraps?, cutting mistakes?) and fish for sushi should not be like that. 

Chef asked in the end if we wanted more fish that we didn't try and it was the tuna seared with charcoal which is $20 a piece - not worth it, it wasn't anything special you just watch them touch the tuna with the hot charcoal (instead of a blow torch) and the tuna cheek, which we also got (hoping we would end the experience on a high note) which I've had elsewhere and this one was not as good, expected much better. It's supposed to be buttery, instead we felt like it had a glaze of oil on top because it actually tasted greasy.

We were only able to get a 9pm bar seat and by the time we were done the staff was cleaning up in front of us, including carrying around garbage and then wiping down the counters (unsanitary), not waiting for us leave, but basically implying that. Oh and they gave us green tea at the very end of the meal... guess they didn't want to keep refilling it throughout the experience. Wish it was as good as the articles noted online but I guess overtime the quality went down. Was really hoping it would at least meet expectations.

So the website is a little misleading - it says sushi omakase is $180 and sushi kaiseki is $225, but it was actually $155/$195 when I went. You can also get a $95/$125 beverage pairing with either.

My party and another we're a few minutes early for our 5:30pm reservation, and the door was... locked. So we stood outside in the awful cold (it was -15C that night) and when 5:30pm hit, I tugged at the entrance door again and this time it yielded. Wonder why the person who unlocked the door didn't peek out to see if anyone was waiting.

Anyway, it's a small space, so there was no entryway for us to hang out anyway. About 15-20 people get seated around a u-shaped sushi bar. They were playing R&B like Beyonce, so contemporary vibes is right.

I rather liked the sushi but I'm not sure the fish was treated the best. Many pieces were overly chewy/ligamentous and to me it didn't seem like much of the fish went through any curing process at all. I did enjoy some of the oilier pieces like the mackerel (which had no funky taste whatsoever), and really liked the palate cleanser of lotus root and shiso leaf. Overall I think I was expecting the sushi to be more creative/unconventional but it was still pretty safe.

That picture you see floating around with toro, uni, caviar and gold leaf? That's a $28 supplement and not part of the omakase.

Anyway, there were about 18 pieces altogether, and I'd say the fish was all very thickly sliced with a little dab of rice... wished there was just a touch more rice, and the rice felt a little hard at times.

Given the wealth of omakase opportunities I'm not sure I'll be coming back. At this price point, I had a much more interactive/engaging/intimate experience with the chef at Kura and Cagen. Sushi Dojo is pretty good too, although the environs aren't as nice as Shuko.

Came here to get the kaiseki and omakase meal. When I first heard that this place takes a twist on the way they do sushi, I was intrigued.

My prediction is that this place will never get a michelin star.

Will break this down into the ambiance/service, the kaiseki portion, and then the omakase portion.

The first thing I noticed was the ambiance. There was a lot of hip hop music in the background, and when you are trying to sit at the sushi bar it's impossible to squeeze in. You HAVE to have someone move the chair back, you take the empty spot the chair was in, and then have the chair be slid into that slot with you in it. Also, while they were taking our order...they were very insistent on having us order the add ons while we order our normal menu. While we were on the omakase, the pacing was awful. The chef had two customers, one being a regular and us. He heavily focused on them and it took sometimes 7 minutes between sushi pieces for us! That really ruined the mood. Also, when eating the sushi, one piece still had a scale in it!!?!?!?!?! What the hell...really?

Now onto the food, first came the kaiseki. They are essentially a couple of fish pieces that were fresh and light. There was also a beef short rib that was one of the most tender pieces I've ever had in my life. Was the kaiseki part worth it? Meh...40 bucks for a couple of dishes that were ok. The really good thing was that they were fillers and otherwise I might've been hungry without them. 

Onto the omakase. The first piece was toro! (what?!!?!?) Usually you don't start out so rich, but they did it because they end even richer. The toro....seemed to be a bit too soft. There's a difference between fatty and soft, and this toro felt like the ground toro one might use in handrolls or something. Was a little bit disappointed with what is usually my favorite piece. Then continued to a bunch of white fish and they are usually pretty traditional. Some didn't have any wasabi in it and very little soy sauce, so it ended up being particularly bland. Eventually we got to one of my favorite pieces of the night, scallops. This was so fresh and it was firm, but yet so soft. That's when the quality of the food started going up. Next came some sweet shrimp, uni, and then the star of the show....grilled toro. Wow that was amazing. So soft and warm and full of umami...just the star of the show. There was also some cod tempura with truffle on it that was interesting and good (the chef did add some uni to it since we were one of the last parties of the night). Lastly, there was this apple pie for dessert that was very unexpected, but very well received.

Coming from San Francisco, maybe the level of service just isn't there in NYC. I thought the service and experience was awful (although they did a great job of filling up my water), the kaiseki wasn't worth it (just eat some mcdonalds before coming), and the omakase wasn't anything too special until the last half of the pieces.

Given how expensive this place was, I cannot comfortably recommend others to come to this place if you are expecting a $200 meal.

As soon as we walked in we were greeted by the host but something seemed off about the environment. The host asked did we have a reservation and we told her no so she said that since we don't have one we can't sit at the bar but at a table in the back. While she's talking to us, I'm assuming but not sure, the manager and another tall male approached us with concern in their eyes and sizing us up. So after that I told my boyfriend that we weren't eating there because from the looks of it they did not want our money. The place is super exclusive and not very welcoming but hey it is New York so yeah.

Amazing ambience and generally very solid food. The sushi very good but not as sublime as many other omakase in the city. However the vibe, music, drink selection and kaiseki variety made up for it. Very good value at $195. And yes the pie was legit.

Amazing!! My husband and I had a wonderful experience at Shuko last night. We came here for my birthday, everything was excellent. Service was top notch, food of course was phenomenal. We ordered the kaiseki menu which includes a 17 piece omakase offering as well as hot and cold dishes.

tl;dr

Once a Michelin star hopeful, but they probably don't deserve a star.

----

I like to write retrospective reviews when there's the luxury of looking back at more than one dinner because it shows me how the restaurant has evolved over time. We came to Shuko twice in the last two years -- both times in the fall, October 2017 and one week ago in November 2018.
