We initially came to Shuko due to murmurs that it was about to get a Michelin star in 2017 (Shuko is a darling of the Eater staff and it gets a LOT of press time by Eater). We didn't want to pay the raised prices post-star, so we booked a last minute reservation before stars were about to be announced (kind of petty, I know ^___^"). It was a great experience. The guys at the helm of Shuko are Masa trained, but they are able to create an avant-garde style of omakase that blends American apple pie and caviar with milk toast with a selection of classical and fusion nigiris.

We did the kaiseki both times (with the wine pairing in 2017, cocktails in 2018). Their most standout dish is their caviar paired with tuna and a piece of delectable milk toast. The milk toast (a stroke of genius since these were the sweet Asian milk toasts I grew up eating :P) combined with the caviar equals immediate insane flavor explosions. The warm dishes are always a mix bag -- in 2017 the standout was the octopus and corn, and in 2018 I enjoyed the truffle chawanmushi amuse immensely (the poached lobster was not bad, I suppose). The nigiri selection contains a healthy dose of the fusion variety with a generous application of tare (soy based sauces) on many of the pieces. Shuko focuses a lot on white fish which I appreciate -- some omakase places are very heavy on tuna and oily fish (salmon, escolar, ocean trout) which tends to trend heavier on the palate. I've found the fish selection for the nigiris to be quite balanced at Shuko - the baby shrimp in 2018 was a pleasant surprise (reminds me a lot of amaebi, but this seems smaller and sweeter?). The wine pairing in 2017 was decent - sake pairing for the nigiris was on-point, the wines for the warm dishes were ho-hum. We opted for cocktails in 2018 and they hit the spot -- given the price differential in the two ($150 for the pairing vs ~$18 each cocktail) it seems like a no-brainer to just go for cocktails.

So after 2017, a solid 4 to 4.5 stars. However, we were disappointed on several counts in 2018 -- the warm dishes all seemed to miss the mark here and there. To give two examples: the dashi in the radish dish was heavy-handed and overly salty. The roast pork belly dish (although not overly fatty which I appreciate) seemed thrown together without much finesse especially with the random large pieces of roasted cabbage. The nigiri course seemed a bit short? (they said 17 pieces but we received 15 including the "palate cleanser" lotus root piece -- in any rate, it was more abbreviated than the 2017 rendition). 

To add insult to the injury, the waiter did not charge me my pre-specified tip. I personally always round the tip so that the final amount comes out to be the closest dollar, but my final bill from Shuko on the credit card contained cents, which means that either the tip was entered in error or it was modified. This is a minor gripe (since I can't remember if I was undercharged/overcharged, or what the difference between what I wrote down and what was on my credit card was). This was probably only the second time it has ever happened to me ever, but this reflects poorly on the professionalism and training of the waitstaff, especially at a fine dining establishment (which, sad to say, was actually one of the highlights of Shuko - the waitstaff is attentive and picks up on the left-handed dining habits of my partner very quickly each time, faster than Sushi by Bou who never realized! haha).

With the 2018 revisit, I must conclude that although I love the ambience and the overall dining experience of Shuko, the food is still not quite ready for the big leagues and the Michelin inspectors are right to not award a star both years. There's room for improvement, and I hope they keep becoming better :)

ps. some people have noted the key is in the add-ons, but with the kaiseki already at $195, i could care less about how good your $60 A5 wagyu is if you can't execute the kaiseki properly. :(

pps. i did not take notes in 2018 so can't remember what a lot of the pieces in the nigiri selections were ^___^"

Shuko is in my opinion one of the best omakase places in New York, taking into account the price, atmosphere, and quality of fish. 

The space is sophisticated and minimalist. Nothing too fancy or scene-y. This allows you to really focus on what's important here - the sushi. 

We got the omakase and weren't expecting the amount of fish we were about to receive (aka make sure you come hungry!) It started off with a few seafood focused cold appetizers, all of which were very light and tasty. This is where the creativity really shines because the chef can incorporate vegetables into the dishes. This properly prepares you for the barrage of fish that is about to come. There were almost 20 pieces in total, encompassing different cuts of tuna, salmon, uni, salmon roe, scallop, shrimp - pretty much everything you can imagine and in all forms (sushi, rolls, etc). Some were more amazing than others but everything was very high quality. Oddly enough, one of my favorites was the truffle mushroom. 

For the price of $155, the omakase at Shuko is highly worth it.

Probably the best sushi joint I've ever been to. Everything is excellent starting with the atmosphere. The restaurant is dominated by a sushi bar where you get to watch the chefs execute their craft. It's classy but not pretentious. Somehow it had a formal feel though there was no need to dress to the nines. Highly recommend the omikase. Each piece is an explosion of different textures, flavors, and temperatures. I never really knew what to expect but there wasn't a course I didn't love - even the sea urchin. To top it off the wine selection is excellent. I tried the French red burgundy (Pinot Noir) and could barely stop drinking. The price isn't for the light of heart (i.e. wallet) but it was totally worth it. Pick a special night and try for yourself.
Great sushi. When I went I happened to be sitting two seats away from Aaron Paul (Jesse from Breaking Bad). The sushi was incredible, the presentation the prep and all. Definitely would go back.

I came here on a Saturday night for dinner with reservations and we were seated immediately. It seems like this place has a strict cancellation fee policy because a patron was arguing with the host about refunding the cancellation fee back to him due to an emergency.

Overall, I thought the sushi courses were great. I won't go into too much detail on each of the 17 pieces but they were all good. Some better than others, but all fresh and well made.

I ordered the sushi kaiseki menu (sushi + some dishes) and I have to say, the Kaiseki part was pretty disappointing. I think the meal would have been better if there were more dishes and less sushi, like other kaiseki places I've been to in the US and Japan. The Sushi Kaiseki is pretty filling though (at least for me). -1 star because I don't think they balanced out the meal very well with 20% dishes and 80% sushi, given that it's supposed to be a kaiseki.

Service was polite and polished, but not too friendly. Overall, I'd recommend the sushi omakase menu here and I'd skip getting the kaiseki add-ons.

This place is a total ripoff and scam. The staff is rude and they will rush you. I heard the manager talking to the waiter about trying to get us out quickly, which is ridiculous when the bill is $455. The fish quality here was just straight up bad and it doesn't take a genius to realize that. I felt like I was eating an average sushi deluxe platter at any sushi joint in nyc, which usually costs $20. I really don't understand this place since it was so highly touted online as one of the top sushi spots in nyc. Maybe they thought they could cut their costs and switch to buying cheap quality fish and get away with it since they now have the reputation, or maybe they are just PR masters who tricked everyone from the start by having flashy celebrities and guests come to their restaurant, I'm not sure. What I am sure about, is that I had to pay a $455 bill for fish that I could've gotten from any average sushi joint. The sushi was chewy, plain, small, dry and didn't have much flavor. They didn't even try to hide the Fish quality with some garnish or maybe some searing. It was plain old fish with maybe a brushing of soy sauce at most. Me and my wife told the manager after about our bad experience and that We were highly disappointed and all he did was give us his business card. Don't go here whatever you do!!!!! Please! Save your money. You're better off going to the reliable and always high quality sushi seki and walking away with a full belly and a $200 check. I wouldn't be surprised if this place goes out of business in the next year. They have nerve and need to make major changes. I just don't know how the people that eat here don't realize this, it's insane and odd!

Beyond impressed with this place. My girlfriends and I tried this discreet place out from another friends recommendation and we couldn't have been happier! It is definitely expensive but worth every dollar and worth the amazing experience. The food was an orgasm in your mouth and it was perfectly filling you don't feel starved or hungry at the end or bloated. There was not one tasting we didn't like and we couldn't find anything bad to say about this place! I would come back and spend double here if it cost that much. It was the highlight of our New York trip.

I came here with my girlfriend for her birthday dinner. 

Shuko is situated and tucked away on 12th street in a very unassuming entrance. When you enter, the space is small but the servers are very attentive. They seat you quickly and watch over you (in an unintrusive way) throughout the meal to see if you need anything and also to clean your space and eating area. 

We ordered the Kaiseki which included the 17-course sushi omakase but also other items which was the owner's interpretation of traditional Japanese cuisine. The dishes were very delicious, however during the sushi courses I would suggest that the chef have a bit more of a deft hand with how much wasabi he includes in each piece of nigiri. In about a fifth of the pieces, there was way too much wasabi which drowned out the other flavors (this was also inconsistent within the pieces as my girlfriend had a similar issue but across different nigiri pieces). 

The one qualm I did have about my experience was that we felt rushed. The hostess let us know that we had to "release" our table by 8:30 because of another guest that was dining. She didn't seem very apologetic about it and borderline rude. 

Overall, I was very glad I had this omakase experience with my girlfriend (it was a very special night), however I would recommend other restaurants for a better and more consistent omakase experience.
This is probably the best meal I have ever had. Definitely for special occasions only as dinner can run you upwards of $700 for two
Fantastic hospitality. Food was fresh, well prepared and delicious. Highly recommend!

Another visit and another wonderful time. I did the supplements this time and although pricey, was definitely worth it. The A5 wagyu was so soft and buttery. The uni, wagyu, caviar piece was super indulgent but the perfect bite. 

And of course, the off collar tuna was great just like last time. It's crazy to imagine that a "trash" cut could be transformed into something so magical.

Fantastic dining experience. We sat at the bar with Chef Jimmy Lau and his apprentices. We got the Kaiseki. Each piece of sushi/dish was divine and perfectly crafted. The atmosphere is a perfect date spot or for special occasions. We were stuffed by the end of it all.

On 12th Street between University Place and Broadway, Shuko situates itself on the block with a minimalistic yet Zen-like exterior, leaving customers to potentially overlook and walk pass the restaurant. It could take a bit of time before you find the entrance and walk through to what seems like the entering of a private event.

It won't be long until the trendy music hits and pulls you in, more closely enwrapping you into the vibe of the restaurant. The wait staff leads you to one of the 20 seats at the sushi counter, forged from unfinished tamo, a type of Japanese ash. There are also seats at tables towards the front of the restaurant.

The Chefs Jimmy Lau and Nick Kim want their guests to feel like as if Shuko is your living room, and that you're enjoying your dinner with nice service and in an enjoyable Zen-like atmosphere. What better way to embrace that than with music, different from the traditional Japanese restaurant, playing slightly louder over dialogues between guests, to mimic the liveliness and ambiance of a family living room? The music is not too loud that it will shadow conversations between guests though.

The personnel at Shuko demonstrated professional service, were well mannered and closely attentive, and detailed enough with serving the food and drinks, but not to the point that it intrudes the connections between the Chef and the guests.

At Shuko, there is only one choice to make - deciding between the sushi omakase or the kaiseki omakase menu. Both omakase menus include is 18 pieces of sushi, however the kaiseki omakase menu includes the addition of five composed dishes, most of which are hot. Sushi Chefs Jimmy Lau and Nick Kim both have a common vision, one that turns away from the norm of high-end sushi establishments. They also play with the traditional understanding and boundaries of what makes up Japanese dining, but at the same time balancing their traditional training and their diverse backgrounds. It is very evident that they successfully achieve this with both of the Chefs' innovative use of ingredients.

To start off our kaiseki omakase (the menu changes often), there were two appetizers. The first is a house-made mochi with shiso and pumpkin squash purée, topped with pumpkin seeds. The purée blended really well with the mochi, while the pumpkin squash would wrap the mochi after every bite. The second appetizer was yellowtail with daikon, shiso, tempura flakes and bonito soy sauce. The fish was so fresh, and the fresh sweet taste of the yellowtail really shined through.

The sushi course begins with a piece of chu toro sushi, which was so fatty that the oil of that piece spills over every surface of your palate. The shima aji had an amazing firm texture and its natural sweetness stood out. The dorade, as Chef Jimmy said, is considered the bacon of the veal in a fish. That basically explains how the fattiness of this fish can cover your palate with a lasting taste and can remind you of otoro. The Sawara (Spanish mackerel) topped with myoga stood out for its texture, resembling the texture of a scallop. The list continues and goes from golden eye snapper to Hirame (fluke) to ocean trout to amber jack to uni, and many more. Chef Jimmy served both Maine and Hokkaido uni. The Maine uni was sweeter and more straightforward with it natural sweetness, whereas the Hokkaido one was a bit more rich and creamy but it took some time to get to its sweet taste, which was not as apparent. The shiitake mushroom tempura topped with shaved truffles was one of the memorable pieces. The warm crunchy exterior gave it an extra layer or flavor, along with the rich and empowering flavor and aroma of the shaved truffles.

What also was different at Shuko was that the chefs would toast the nori (seaweed) right in front of you before they use it to serve the hand roll. They have a little charcoal fire to prepare the nori to-order, making sure that each handroll is served with a crunch and that the seaweed creates a slight toasted aroma and adding another flavor to the handroll.

After the sushi course but right before the dessert, the chef serves shiso wrapped with a pickled lotus root, a taste cleanser to awaken your taste buds for dessert. The dessert was The Granite, a Concord grape sorbet with slight hints of lime. Another dessert was a slice of apple pie with burnt bay leaf sided with a scoop of soba ice cream. The top layer of the apple pie was crunchy, something you would expect from the crust. The soba ice cream was extremely creamy and it balanced out really well with the pie. A cup of genmaicha tea was served, and was so potent in its rich rice flavor. This calls for the perfect ending of a sushi dinner as the aromas of the tea runs through your nose with each sip of the tea.

Getting past its minimal façade is when you will find the true beauty of it Zen-like dining experience and environment accompanied with perfectly crafted dishes and sushi.

Shuko is very small and intimate restaurant - there were maybe 12 bar seats and a few small tables. Even the entrance was a bit hidden, it doesn't look like a restaurant from the outside. The ambience was quiet and cozy up until more people started to fill in the seats - their music playlist is also very weird. For a classy restaurant like this, they were playing club music and it honestly was funny. 

We decided to do the omakase kaiseki ($195 pp). The courses before the sushi were interesting - I wasn't impressed with most of them. My favorite dish was probably the grilled octopus that was paired with such an interesting sauce. Since I've had sushi from Japan before, my standards may be a little high. My favorite part of the omakase was the tuna straight from the bone and the fresh squid. I felt like the omakase was never ending - was so full at the end! The chef and staff were all professional and nice. To be honest, the dessert is what made my night because I love ice cream - "apple pie with a scoop of roasted soba ice cream" was amazing. I've never had soba ice cream before and it was an interesting concept - all homemade!

I highly recommend coming to Shuko for an omakase experience!
Nice decor, but the place has an insect problem.  Staff was notified but they do not seem to care.

Shuko is a total rip off. We got the Omakase and the fish isnt even special. At $155 I expect more for an Omakase; no soup and laughable appetizer! The restaurant relies ont he fact that the two head chef used to work at Masa, but in this case it means nothing! Because I've been to joints with better sushi for half the price. The whole ambience just feels so pretentious. Please do yourself a favor a look elsewhere. Plenty of omakase spot in nyc, this is not one of them that's worth going.

I was very excited to go to shuko for the first time, but i was very disappointed after the meal. Each piece was small and tasted mundane. There was no ebi, no tomago, etc! 

I would not recommend coming...

We came on a Saturday night for kaiseki for 3 and were fairly impressed with the offerings and the overall meal. The door to the restaurant isn't easy to spot, we missed it at first glance - very subtle, and the interior is quaint. We had reserved a table off the bar for the night but the entire restaurant tables and chef's table/bar were full the entire night.
We chose the kaiseki offering and also ordered the 'drop the mic' and the 'wagyu beef hand roll' off the ad hoc menu. One at our table ordered the pairing with the meal as well.
Overall the food was delicious and fish super fresh. We were certainly full by the end of the meal. A few notes to point out:
- Sushi offerings that came plated could have been better presented. Some plates nigiri was falling over onto others, some plates not in a neat straight row. It just takes away from the overall presentation when it isn't visually pleasing
- All of the fish was amazing except the uni. Surprising, but we've had way better uni in many other places. Not sure what it was, but the uni was just not good
- Dessert - wish we had been offered an alternative. I would have been happy with just 2 scoops of the delicious soba ice cream, as I absolutely hate apple pie
Overall the meal was a success - we spent almost 3 hours in the restaurant!
I don't usually eat sushi (I sense your judgement already) but this place has unquestionably won me over. Highest quality fish from Hokkaido uni to some seasonal catch delivered overnight from Japan.

While I find your lack of interest in accommodating vegetarians and vegans hysterical, I have to ask, who the Hell do you think you are, Shuko? If you're going to have the (fish) balls to serve only omakase, you'd damn well better have great omakase. 
You do not. 
In the 3 times I've visited (forced twice by family) I have had 3 plates I would want again. I will not return, even under duress. There are hipsters who can be talked into thinking anything is good who need that seat far more than I.
Best sushi omakaze in NYC. This is a must visit for anyone who enjoys good quality sushi.

I'm sitting here trying to figure out why this average Joe omakase spot has hit a 4 star review on Yelp. I just don't get it. 

Maybe it was the night I dined it or the fact we sat at a table but I would NOT rate this 4 stars especially comparative to the price my date paid. 

My date wanted to come here as a first date & I was like YASSS because I had this place bookmarked for quite some time. I was excited but also skeptical. 

The door is hidden. There's literally no sign labeling the restaurant & the restaurant is small. Think two tables and bar seating only. It's super intimate but this sushi restaurant doesn't match their ambiance with their music selection. I was laughing the whole night especially when I heard Cardi B come on for a brief moment. Sushi and Cardi B? OOH, ok I guess they're down to get ratchet here. 

There are two omakase options & a menu for add ons. 

Our omakase started off with this barely edible Asparagus "soup" as claimed by the staff. It's a small petri-esque dish, cold & garlicy AF. Mind you, I LOVE garlic but this dish was just plain out weird. My date agreed. We took one bite and said NEXXXXT. 

Every single sushi piece was over powered with sauce. Like, can I please taste the fish? I get it. Sometimes the chef pairs sushi pieces with flavors to complement the fish. I guess our chef was feeling salty bc ours was OVERLY salty.  And I know it wasn't just me because yes, my date agreed. 

Every single sushi piece had me reaching for sake. SALTINESS OVERLOAD. 

To finish off the meal they served a refreshing sorbet. But really, how can you mess up sorbet? 

All in all, while the sushi could probably have tasted effin' amazing, I will never know. Texture wise, yes it was expensive grade. But c'mon how you gonna hide that taste with an OVER powering sauce??? 

Would I recommend or come back? Nope. Don't do it. It's not worth it. Steer clear. Go elsewhere. Not worth it. I can recommend another that's worth your money & time.

Side note: If I had paid for our $400+ meal (we also ordered a few bottles of sake) I would have been very upset. My date saved this restaurant from a solid 2 star review.

One star because my wife didnt have to order "shari sho" because the nigiri are pretty small compared to say 15 East, Jewel Bako, Kanoyama, Noda, Shoji.  Service was okay, but overall a pretty lackluster meal at this price point.  At this price range, no anago, or tamago, no seasonal fish like shiraebi, or fish from japan.

Excellent sushi- living in Seattle we have some of the best sushi and I've found many NYC spots to be ok at best in comparison. Shuko was a welcome exception to that and really impressed me. The chef was friendly (but not too overbearing), the food was fantastic. I highly recommend it!

Unfortunately i did not had a horrible experience here, the omakase plus the wagyu beef roll were excellent, enjoyed every moment of the food experience all the way up to our sake pairing except for that one piece towards the end, mint leaves wrapped in a lotus root roll. Melt in your quality nigiri, i was speechless when that 1st piece entered my mouth.

Hubby and I came here to celebrate our one year anniversary and we left determined to make Shuko our new anniversary tradition!

We made a reservation for Sunday at the sushi counter and were quite confused when GoogleMaps and Yelp kept insisting that Shuko would be closed when we got there. However, we put our faith in the confirmation email we received and confirmed when we got there that although Shuko used to close every Sunday, they are now OPEN ON SUNDAYS (5:30-9:30) FOR SUSHI OMAKASE ONLY ($155). This meant that although we were had our hearts set on the Sushi Kaiseki, it was not available. However, we still loved our experience, had such a fun time chatting with Jimmy-san and our sushi chef, Ry, savored every amazing bite of sushi, and we can't wait to return for the Kaiseki menu next time!

We started out by selecting one of the hot dishes that was available as an add on that evening: a flavorful and tender red prawn paired with a salad of snow pea pod stems (aka my favorite vegetable in the world). I always feel a little stressed at nice restaurants where the price is not presented to you (and you feel too embarrassed to ask). For my fellow frugal-foodies who are trying to blend in with the fancy people, the price on this one turned out to be $35 (not too bad).

As for the omakase itself, hubby and I both agreed that it was our best omakase experience yet (including the one we did in Japan on our honeymoon).

Over the course of 2 hours, we enjoyed:
+ Egg custard with mushroom and roe
+ Hamachi with shiso, daikon, and miyoga
+ ~17 pieces of sushi - I lost count... The most memorable two for me were the toro that we started with and the uni, which was the sweetest uni I've had in recent memory/had ever (thinking about it makes me want to cry a little...)
- Uni caviar toro sushi - As our omakase came to an end, we were asked if we wanted to add anything and I simply couldn't resist (especially seeing as the toro and uni were my favorite pieces!) However, the saying is true that there really can be too much of a good thing because sadly, I didn't feel like I was able to taste each component in this piece and would've been happier with just uni. This add-on was also another case of a surprise-me-at-the-end-with-the-price and it turned out to be $28/piece--eep!
+ Strawberry granita - This was soooo refreshing and yummy!
+ Apple pie (on the house) in celebration of our anniversary! (Thanks!!)

I believe this is the worst and the most expensive Japanese restaurant I ever dined at. I had dinner with my family on the 16th May the suhi is just unbearable, service horrible unforgettable experience. I have dined in some of the best up scale restaurants in Tokyo, Hong Kong, Bangkok, singapore and london to name a few. The whole family got sick afterwards as the sushi was quite fishy ad quality is way sub standard. I strongly advise guests to dine at any fast food Japanese bar.

I dined with my family at Shuko in May of 2018 for dinner. I believe it was one of the worst and the most expensive Japanese food I have ever had. I've dined in many upscale Japanese restaurants worldwide in Tokyo, Singapore, Bangkok, Hong Kong and London to name a few. 

Moreover, we all got very sick after our experience there due to the fishiness and lack of quality of the food. I wouldn't recommend this restaurant to anyone.

Shuko takes reservations up to two weeks in advance.  I came here for my boyfriend's birthday since he's been wanting to try this place for a while now.  We got omakase and loved the uni, needlefish, scallop, botan ebi (separate order), and a few others, but I can't remember the names.  I believe it was my first time having needlefish so I can't really compare it anything.  
I admit, I have had better omakase where they experimented more and/or had better choices of fish like whyyy the tuna roll, but the service makes me give them 5 stars.  Our servers and sushi chef were kind and attentive.  Our sushi chef was easy to talk to and our servers refilled our beverages without us asking, which made this relaxing after work. 
I told our server it was my boyfriend's birthday so she could include a candle with our dessert.  Although it wouldn't have been possible to put a candle on the desert that was part the omakase (it was icy) and of course I didn't know since I wasn't paying attention oops.  We got a complimentary birthday dessert - apple pie with ice cream on the side!  Yummm I probably had most of it.  It was also very sweet of Chef Jimmy Lau to stop what he was doing to come over to wish my boyfriend a happy birthday.  My boyfriend and I will definitely return due to the friendly service here at Shuko!  Thank you for making it memorable.

An outrageously disrespectful manager with no client service skills asked as to leave the restaurant while we were still having wine, because "other guests were coming in"! At 10pm. While the restaurant closes at 10:30!

And all this happened after we paid more than $250 per person. When we told him it was not ok, all he had to say was "thank you for your feedback" and when we called the restaurant, the same manager kept lying about the restaurant policy. What next seating are you talking about, if the restaurant closes in 30min and it's a 13 meal course? Disgusted and humiliated!

If you want to pay $250 for 12 pieces of sushi and some strawberry flavored ice and be asked to leave (as if you are in your next door pizzeria), come here. Otherwise, go to Kappo Masa or Zuma and get much tastier food and some level of respect and client service. I would put 0 stars if I could. Never posted a review, but this time I just couldn't keep silent.

Came here for my birthday. The chef and service was great however the food itself was underwhelming especially for the price point. You do get a lot of different courses and will definitely be full by the end of it tho.
Hands down the best sushi experience I've ever had. Each piece was uniquely delicious and the service was incredible. Totally worth the price.

After having a bad experience at another omakase today, I wasn't feeling satisfied. So I was hearing great thing about Chef Jimmy Lau and his Omakase I decided to go try them out. What a great decision that was even tho I didn't a have reservation chef was able to squeeze me in. My omakase meal was 155 pp. The service and food was great. Chef Lau was an awesome host, make sure I had great food and wonderful experience. A must try Omakase in NYC

My hubby took me there for our 10 year anniversary.  Nice atmosphere. I like the way they present their sushi.. price is on the higher side but you get full afterward.  Some places charge high price but then you need another meal to get full. 
All the sushi PCs are fresh but there is one that I think is 5 star by itself. Crispy nori, lightly torched toro w Thai chilli sauce.. I clap right after I finish this piece... it's simple but amazing.  I wish there are more pieces like this..  
Service top of the notch..

Very B&T. Ran out of grapefruit mix for the martini. Seated a couple next to larger and obnoxious party in small section that is walled off so they could not be ignored. Should not happen for a $600 dinner.

The restaurant is decorated in a very contemporary Japanese minimalist aesthetic with a lovely wood bar table. The fish is extremely fresh and My best sushi experience. Their scallops and uni were my personal highlights of the night and they offer a great sake list as well. In addition, the price point is amazing (a little over 200/person omakase) considering how spectacular the food is. There is no sacrifice of quality for price.

It's a cute place for a omakase type of restaurant - bigger than many little omakase only restaurants. Their customer service is amazing - from the moment you walked in to when you left. 
We decided to order the kaiseki and we felt divided about the food. The cooked food they brought out was delicious - however the fish they served I felt was way under par. I've been to many omakase restaurants in NYC of all price points and for the cost- it was extremely disappointing. If we just had the omakase instead of the kaiseki we would have been even more disappointed. There were several pieces that were a bit dry! and bland (although waiter - pointed that we didn't need to add soy to most of it). For the price - I would not return.

I had a good time here with bar seats, but was a bit underwhelmed especially for the price point of the kaiseki meal. Everything was fresh, but nothing wowed me except for the toro. Was extremely full though.

Shuko gets the honor of being my first-ever omakase experience. Most if not all of my sushi-eating experiences have been of the casual variety. Mostly of the Seamless variety, actually. It's funny, I love dining out and have explored the NYC restaurant scene extensively, but have oddly not been to any upscale Japanese restaurants yet. It's certainly a unique experience. I've been hesitant to write this review because I feel like I should be judging my experience based on a frame of reference that I have not yet acquired. I felt like I should've been blown away and while our experience was great, there wasn't anything I'd necessarily say was exceptional. It's possible I'm just very very accustomed to a specific type of dining and this was different. Shuko's made a lot of prestigious lists and is certainly in Pete Wells's good graces, so its clearly doing something right! The fish was varied and fresh, the starters and finishers were interesting and flavorful, the service was as good as I've experience and the price, well, it's to be expected. 

Came here at 6pm on a Saturday night. If you want a weekend reservation, be sure to look at Resy at least a few weeks in advance. The space itself is quite small and most seating is at the bar/sushi counter, so it's limited. Regardless of when you arrive, be sure to leave yourself a good two hours for Omakase, maybe three for Kaiseki. The dishes come out pretty rapid fire but as you hopefully know, you will be receiving a lot of things. I found the pace to be almost too quick at times, so I took it upon myself to slow down and savor each course to let the experience sink in.

Much of the allure here--and I'm not sure if this is consistent with other Omakase spots or unique to Shuko--are the element of surprise and mystique. It starts even before you sit down: the restaurant is unmarked, just a sleek door accompanied by a building number. Walking inside, you need to first pass through a velvet curtain before shedding your coats and getting seated. They do provide menus, but much of the description you'll find accompanies the beverages. They have a decent cocktail and wine menus, as well as a nice Japanese whiskey selection. Other than that, you're basically given the choice of going with Omakase at $135/pp or Kaiseki at $175/pp, with the option for a few a la carte add-ons (a Wagyu beef was on our a la carte menu, for example). You receive the same sushi tasting with both meals. The main difference is what precedes the meal: I believe you receive two dishes prior to the sushi courses when you choose Omakase, and seven dishes prior to the sushi when you choose Kaiseki. 

Regardless of which route you choose, they don't provide you with any sort of preview of what you'll be receiving as part of the pre fixe. And unlike at many other tasting-only spots, you won't receive a list of what you received that night upon leaving. They say that because the menu changes so frequently here, they pretty much don't have literature on what one could/did receive on any given night. Minor gripe because I enjoy reflecting on/recounting/remembering/better understanding my dining out experiences, but oh well.

Once you've chosen whether to go Omakase or Kaiseki (we went Omakase to save a bit), the meal starts almost immediately. The first two dishes were fun, creative and tasty. They also made conceptual sense in terms of prepping up for the sushi we'd be receiving. The first was an egg custard with mushrooms and roe, the second was a crab salad. Both light but still super flavorful. 

The sushi itself was simple for the most part, and all very fresh. A few more creative rolls closer to the end, but most of what we experienced was a superb variety of fish/seafood. Some of our favorites were a trout, a sweet shrimp (apparently only in season for 3-4 weeks out of the year), the uni (I mean, how could you not collapse over this), and a few others that I fail to remember specific names for. All nigiri except for those few rolls at the end (with the most delicious seaweed I've ever consumed, I might add). I seriously regret not bringing a pen and paper with me, if for no other reason than to mark down the most esoteric types of fish one rarely/never sees elsewhere.

Two more nice touches:
-They lightly paint the sushi with soy sauce/wasabi--no dunking/dousing here
-Before receiving any sushi, they'll give you both store-bought ginger as well as homemade ginger, so you can taste the difference. As expected, fresh ginger wins--our tastebuds are more sophisticated than we tend to realize.

While finishing our palette cleanser, I decided I'd allow myself one whiskey despite the price. I love whiskey but don't know much about Japanese whisky and Shuko seemed like a decent place to dip my toe in. After telling the bartender what I tend to like, he recommended Ichiro's Malt and Grain Blended Whisky. Though it didn't blow my mind, it was still yummy, very smooth and a great way to finish the meal.

Simply Perfection in a Dining Experience.!!
The entire two hours we spent at the Bar was such a total delight..
Shuko definitely nailed it for me on my typically demanding checklist...~
The Food..Omakase Option..OMG..it was absolutely a non stop, sequential taste treat ..one serving after another..thoughtfully diverse and surprising..impactful yet balanced..
I rightly expected, at this price, for the highest quality ingredients and preparation..and wow.. did they deliver beyond ..

But what impressed me the most ?..the people and their flawless attention to SERVICE!~The staff is so well trained in the most minute details ( I'm clumsy..my fallen napkin ( 2x ) reappeared freshly  and with seemingly stealth efficiency by my side ).  
My  little drop of sauce on the Wooden bar surface..Bingo ..gone by the dude who is there to keep the beautiful wooden surface always clean.*  The Sommelier ..such a pro..he treated my guest to tasting just about anything she inquired about to educate and inform her experience beyond the description of words..
The Sushi chef is right in front of you..and you can't help but participate in the intimacy of the preparation. It also helps when this person is so friendly and accessible when called upon. ( think Japanese...its like a dance..or a polite ritual).
So..if I had the budget.. I would be there 2x a month ..it is that good..trust me.

* as an architect, and furniture buiIder, I was so impressed by the design, lighting, and especialy the unvarnished silky smooth pure wooden bar..when you put your hands on it , it has the delightful warm tactile feel of a master furniture carpenters work. And I know how hard it is to maintain unprotected wood because oil and liquid will soak and stain. But there was a dedicated "cleaner" of any such intrusions.  When I complimented him on his duties, he told me he sands and hand polishes the precious raw wood every day to help it live and breathe. Seriously, foodies, rejoice because this is an intentional detail of your experience at Shuko.

Where to begin. Absolutely amazing Omakase. If your up for high end sushi tasting experiences, this place really is up there. Owners are present to personally ensure quality control of sushi and also the customer satisfaction. There are sommeliers to pair your wine or sake, and they have an exhaustive selection of Japanese whisky. So the liquor component is not overlooked at this omakase venue. They have a $130 and $180 approx omakase option. Can't go wrong with either. One rarity here is that they use actual real coals to sear the sushi. They pick special wood to heat the coals. It's all very thought out. Everything here is well thought out. If you're into Omakase, check this place out. It's not cheap but for this category this place hits the top on all factors of quality, freshness, customer service. Shout out to JJ our server and Jimmy - best chef, and part owner, who takes full pride in running the show and is a true expert. Shuko! Come check it out.

This was a great experience and a decent Sushi Kaiseki. However, the fish selection was fairly average and in turn lead to disappointment for the price me and my group paid. 

All the food that I was highly excited for ended up being average in taste. The uni, the salmon, the tuna. All average. I've had better for cheaper. 

But what truly almost ruined the experience was the final piece which was deemed a "palette cleanser". It was lotus wrapped with a sort of mint leaf. As soon as we bit into it, I almost gagged. A member of my group even whispered to me "do we have to swallow it?"

Whoever set up the menu for this should seriously reconsider the selection. For the price I paid, I was highly disappointed.

I found myself forgetting that I wasn't in an alley way in Kyoto eating at a cozy izakaya. The attention to detail of the food is spectacular and the combination of exotic ingredients, yuzu foams and uni mayonnaise etc. keep the night exciting. The only caveat to this is, for the price Nyc has a lot more offers banging for your buck. Good for dates but not much else.

This is definitely one of my favorite next to Nakazawa, good service and more of a laid back ambience. Fish is ALWAYS on point and the chef do a very good introduction. I've been there a couple of times and never been disappointed.  It can be difficult getting bar reservation but it's definitely worth the experience.

Beyond words. I love the location and ambience of this place. From the outside you can't really see what this place is. I love the fact that there were no signs, makes it more of a mystery. You walk in and meet with a hostess, she opens the curtains to this beautiful restaurant that plays the latest hip-hop hits. We were seated at the bar, with a spectacular view of all the chefs. We ended up getting the larger tasting menu. It was a lot of dishes, so make sure you come hungry. The presentation of each dish is a work of art, each dish had its own identity. Each serving was very well seasoned and in some cases cooked to perfection.

This was a pleasant surprise.  There are very few tables and a long sushi bar so you better be fewer than four unless you reserve the private room.  The service was impeccable and the food genuine and delicious.  You have to be able to eat anything to make the experience worth while.  This is not the place for a picky eater.

Came here a few weeks back for my friend's birthday. We did the kaiseki since it's a must recommended. The ambience of the restaurant was nice. Waitstaff was on top of things and very nice to us. Service and pacing of the time we were there was almost 2 hours. I'm glad we didn't feel rushed and enjoyed the full experience of the meal. I would say try the kaiseki just because you may not feel full from the omakase. I believe we had 21 plates. I think by #17 we started to struggle. Both of us couldn't finish our apple pie a la mode. As much as we liked the experience not everything was entirely amazing. There were a few stand dishes the like tuna toast, toro, uni and some beef handroll that melted in your mouth. Otherwise some of the fishes were okay but tasted really fresh. It's worth a try but I'm sure everyone has their own opinion

Shuko absolutely exceeded my expectations and blew my friend and I away!  I made a reservation through Resy exactly 2 weeks prior to the dinner date.  Unfortunately, all the bar seats were gonna so I settled for a table instead.

Once you enter through an unmarked door, the hostess is right there to take your coat (if you want to do coat check).  My friend and I were seated promptly and were presented with warm hand towels.  Our waitress took her time to explain the menu to us and we decided to go with the Sushi Omakase which was $135.00.  

The Sushi Omakase came with 17 pieces of sushi, 2 appetizers, 1 palette cleanser and a dessert.  For the price and portion... it is TOTALLY worth it!  The 2 appetizers we had were japanese egg custard and hamachi - both were great in terms of flavor.  All the sushi pieces we had were great but we thought the clam was a little too fishy and the scallop wasn't the freshest of the bunch.  I also thought the Hokkaido uni was AMAZING - the portion of uni to rice was perfection!  Our palette cleaner consisted of a rolled up lotus root with shiso leaves inside and this was sooooo refreshing.  Our dessert was blood orange, vanilla, tapicoa served in a dainty little champagne glass.  We were then served with tea which we loved because it was so aromatic!

The service here is EXCELLENT and they really know how to make you feel comfortable as a guest.  Their bathroom is very roomy and they have Aesop soap and lotion which is always a plus (I mean who doesn't like a boujee brand?!).  I would definitely recommend Shuko if you want to try omakase for a decent price!  I am going to come back for sure!!!

Very good. Only reason it gets 4 stars is due to value. You can eat at other sushi restaurants of high quality for less. Ever since coming back from Japan our standards have been raised. We enjoyed everything we ate here. The dishes were interesting and the service was excellent. This restaurant has perhaps an overkill of staff members. The only thing that left me underwhelmed was the dessert which was a grape crushed ice. Tasted just like a Welch's popsicle crushed up.

I came here with my sister while she was visiting in town and this was such a great experience!   The chefs and staff were very friendly and one of the owners worked next to our chef. 

The food itself was delicious! We had the omakase and ordered extra pieces at the end. There were many stand outs. We also didn't feel completely stuffed and gross at the end.  

I enjoyed shuko more than morimotos and would definitely return.  I've actually passed by it many times before but never realized the unmarked door.

One of the best meals I've ever had. We did the Sushi Kaiseki for $175 per person which came with so much food that I unfortunately couldn't finish it all. Every item was amazing and I loved the variety between hot kitchen items and sushi that's made at the counter right in front of you. The door to the restaurant is unmarked so it is a little tough to find. The restaurant itself is quite small with a sushi bar seating around 20 or so people and a table off to the side for a small party. I would definitely recommend sitting at the bar as it's very interesting to watch the chefs prepare the different items. The menu appears to be seasonal and we were given the option between the larger tasting or a smaller sushi tasting. There was also a small section with around 5 add ons to choose from. This restaurant is expensive but it's definitely worth the price.

One of the best Japanese dining experiences I've had thus far. Make reservations and ask for the bar. My boyfriend and I decided to get the $175 Sushi Kaiseki dinner (might as well go all out while we're here).

This included...
- Canape: Brussel sprouts with dried bonito flakes.
- Sunomono: Fresh crab & cucumber salad.
- Bread: Homemade milk bread with toro & caviar. One of my favorites of the night.
- Sashimi:Yellowtail with daikon. Don't usually like daikon but I finished every bite.
- Robata: Scallops & romanesco with hollandaise. 
- Meat: Duck breast.
- Dashi: Mushroom soup.
- Sushi Tasting: The best part. 16 tastings of nigiri. All delicious and masterfully crafted in front of us. I didn't want this to end.
- Granite: Palate cleanser of lime and grape granita. 
- Apple Pie: Not the best apple pie ever, but the ice cream was amazing.

Aside from the food, service was beyond hospitable. The atmosphere was modern but not stuffy (loved how they played loud hip hop music all night). I still dream of this meal and would highly recommend to anyone living in or visiting New York.

Food quality - 5
Great quality sushi, very capable and friendly chefs.
Atmosphere - 2
High stools that are too close together, makes seating feel cramped and awkward.  Not as high-end an atmosphere as I anticipated (lighting, music, etc).  If you're a 'total bro' you will love this place and probably come in fist-bumping the sushi chefs when you sit down (which...DISGUSTING...they are making people's food with their bare hands and you're insisting on touching them?!)
Service - 4 
At times the service of the omakase seemed rushed.  At one point I had barely swallowed one piece and the next one was already on my plate.  In general the servers were friendly and attentive.
Host/GM - 1
Meal nearly ruined due to being 'greeted' by a catty and self-important host/GM at the front door.
Pricey but well worth it. The tasting had a mix of cooked delicacies and lots of innovative sushi (divine!).  The drinks were also fantastic and original.  Service and ambiance perfect.
Great service and great food! Every single piece was super fresh and melty. I cannot begin to express how good it was. Just look at my food pics!
Such delicious, fresh, and simple sushi, my mouth is watering just thinking about it. Excellent service and a few celeb sightings while at dinner :)

After having watched a video of this location being opened by a Masa-trained chef, I was really excited. We opted for the $135 pp omakase, which includes 15 pieces of Nigiri, two amuse bouche, and one dessert. The first amuse bouche was a mochi dish, which I actually wasn't too much a fan of. I thought it was too chewy, and the ingredient (bean I believe?) they put on top was too salty. The second amuse bouche was probably one of my favorite items out of the entire omakase. It was a smoked fish dish and was flavorful, yet also extremely light and fresh. It was a great way to begin the meal. During the actual omakase, we had a total of 15 pieces, such as red snapper, toro, and uni. I really enjoyed all of them, some more than others, except for the squid. However, I did feel that the chef was too quick in serving us the pieces. We felt rushed, almost. While we were eating one piece, he'd begin preparing the next, and sometimes before we had finished one piece, he'd already have the next piece on our plate. For our last piece, we had a fried mushroom, which I found to be interesting and different, but I probably would have preferred fish. We also received a roll that appeared to taste like wagyu. At the very end of the omakase, we each got half a cut up roll of a tuna roll. While it was good for a tuna roll, at the end of the day, it is just a tuna roll. For dessert, we had a frozen grape ice, which I really enjoyed. It was very refreshing. 

In all, I do think it's possible to find much cheaper omakases in the city, for the same or even better quality. I had really wanted to try Shuko because it seemed to be becoming really popular nowadays. However, while Shuko's omakase is good, its price to pleasure ratio isn't as great as many of its other competitors. The $135pp omakase set ended up being approximately $170pp, and we had each gotten a green tea as well. At the end of the meal, I was full, but I wasn't stuffed either. My biggest complaint is just that the meal seemed to be going by too quickly and the pieces weren't exactly all melt-in-your-mouth and mind-blowing, which I was expecting for the price.

Rub your hands against the counter as you're eating - it's one of the smoothest surfaces I've ever touched in my life (and my ex had nice skin!)

Took a friend out for kaiseki when I was in NYC - we both got new jobs and I wanted to ball out a little and spend some quality time together, something we haven't been able to do since college.

Overall, a great meal. Service was impeccable, the chefs were very courteous and the food was high caliber. The vibe is definitely different if you are familiar with omakase, it's more of a hip ambiance rather than the quieter zen experience at other places. Rap music playing in the background. Very busy with many people behind the chef's table. Dimmer lighting, with almost a french-meets-japanese feel to the place.

However, a few gripes. I'm not sure that the dinner was worth what I paid - $175 pp + $125 for wine and sake pairing is a little higher than what I would have priced the meal at. My measuring stick is Wako in SF - they have a tasting menu for $135 with a similar mix of sushi and cooked dishes but some of the fish Wako used was better. The amount of food was surely enough, however, and I left the restaurant full. It was also interesting how they started the nigiri portion of the meal with toro, something very rich and fatty and then moved on from there. This goes in contrast to what I'm used to at other omakase restaurants.

Considering this is the first and only omakase I've had at NYC, I would say it was worth the experience. Their take on the cuisine was unique and executed well, just be ready to shell out to come here.

I've done a lot of kaiseki and omakase in LA and SF and this place by far has been the best tasting one yet. Chef Jimmy's ability to elevate all of his nigiri is absolutely astounding. Every dish he serves is well executed by his team. His team really understands the profile of every fish they serve and it's compliment. Not one mediocre dish which is almost unheard of when doing kaiseki / omakase. 

What I love about this place is that Jimmy and his team are extremely friendly and cognizant of every diner in the restaurant. I am know a fan of uni from Maine! Who would've thought it was taste better than uni from Santa Barbara and Hokkaido. Definitely need to try it! Also, this place is reasonably priced in comparison to LA and SF. My girlfriend and I did the kaiseki with a bottle of sake + 300ml additional and it was under $500. This meal in SF would've costed on average about $1K.

Really unfortunate. I was really looking forward to a meal at Shuko since there's no way I'm ever going to be able to afford Masa and the chefs here are ex-Masa. Overall, I was really disappointed at the quality of the fish, and parts of the service left a lot to be desired. 

My friends and I got a bar seat for 3 and ordered the kaiseki since we had heard really good things about the food here. Bar service and the waiters that came with the kaiseki food was all pretty decent - the service was roughly on par with what I might expect from an aspiring single star restaurant. The dishes left a bit more to be desired. My favorite kaiseki dish was the toro + caviar and milk bread. That was an awesome take on a bread dish, but the other pieces were really just meh. There was a fluke sashimi dish that supposedly had ponzu but really just tasted like dry fish with some salad greens. The short rib dish was good and reminded me more of Thanksgiving meal, but honestly, nothing here was particularly amazing. I was intrigued at the French influences that inspired the dishes here - e.g. a hollandaise sauce that accompanied scallops, but overall, this food was prob at a 3.5 or 4 star range. 

The omakase was the biggest bummer of this meal - for both quality of fish and sushi chef. Fish wise, I was really surprised at how low quality some of the pieces were. I'm not a sushi expert by any means, but I've eaten quite a bit of sushi and I've never had a piece of Spanish mackerel that was creamy in my mouth. Honestly, a lot of the pieces here were comparable to what I can get for much cheaper prices in neighborhood sushi joints, and that's not what you're paying $175 for. They also used Maine uni as opposed to Hokkaido or Santa Barbara (apparently because the other places did not have high quality uni at this time) which again, I suppose is possible since I don't know the industry, but I also know that I had great Hokkaido and Santa Barbara uni a week or so ago at some other sushi establishments, so I was surprised that they served Maine uni, which wasn't particularly fresh. In general, I was surprised about how they neglected to share the origins of any of the fish pieces here, which is something really rare in sushi restaurants who are really proud of sharing where their food is sourced from. Given that, I was a bit dubious of the origins of these pieces. 

The other annoying part of this sushi bar experience was that our chef was a bit patronizing throughout the meal - again, at a $175, or rather $250 post tip and tax point, patronizing service is really annoying. Our chef insisted that my friends and I looked like we were in colleges (maybe complimentary, meh) and then at some point we used the towels to wipe our faces, and while I suppose that may be off from proper sushi etiquette, I just feel like at that price point, to be laughed at represents a bit of a faux pas service wise. 

Overall, really really expensive and no where near the quality or service bar at other omakases in the city. That being said, I will say the apple pie at the end was my favorite dish, but apple pie being my favorite dish at a kaiseki? Yikes.
Incredible experience.  The meal was elegantly  constructed,  prepared and served.  The restaurant has a nice up beat but warm vibe.  Will definitely go back!

Overall, little disappointed. 3.5-4 Sushi was ok above average. If you like to experience good sushi, then go to Sushi Gari, Onodera or Yasuda etc. Shuko is pretty good but definitely one level below their sushi quality. Similar to O Ya, but I think O Ya is one level better than Shuko. O Ya is pretty good but not highly recommended either. Shuko's kaisaki was average. Just okay. 3 at the best. Over priced. However, their wine and sake pairing was excellent! Great selections and generous portions. They pour sake in a wine glasses. When I asked why, they said they have more wine glasses. Not very professional. I want my sake in a real sake glasses if I am paying $600 sake pairings for 4 people. Sake was great but service was Disappointing. No real interaction at the sushi counter like other Edo Mae Sushi place. Great decor and interior. Overall, Not highly recommended.

Came to Shuko to celebrate a friend's birthday and from beginning to end it did not dissapoint. Attentive service and an eclectic music mix set the tone for an fantastic evening and probably the best sushi I've experienced. Amberjack and coal-seared toro were highlights -- absolute perfection. My dinner companion, a NYC foodie and possessing of a palate elevated much higher than mine rated it among her best experiences as well.

My daughter and I visited this restaurant a year ago. Recently we were considering returning, which prompted me to express my lingering sentiments from the original experience. The food was excellent and the atmosphere unique, and I am glad we went there. However, I also feel that it was overpriced at pris fixe of $135 and $175 (without additional pricy items or beverages) being the only options. As I recall, there was no a la carte. Only those two choices were available. By the time tax and tip are added, it is easily $200 per person. To me, it was not worth it in comparison to other restaurant experiences in that price range. We are not going back this year.

Singularly the best dinner I have ever had. My better half did an amazing job scoping out the reservations and snagging one at the bar which is by far the best spot to be, especially if you are a couple. If part of a bigger group of four, I think one of the tables is smarter. 

We did the omakase and believe me it is plenty of food! Started off with a bang and lots of interesting and classic preparations. Ended with an add-on or two as we were just so completely impressed with the main omakase portfolio that we wanted to try a little more exotic stuff. I had some barracuda which I don't recall ever even seeing on a menu. Worth it. 

We did the wine/sake pairing which was also excellently paced and delicious. Started with some champagne and a series of different sakes with ever more interesting stories and tastes. Highly recommended! I mean you are letting the chef handle the food, why not let him handle the beverages as well and get on cruise-control to nirvana. 

Service was perfect. Our waiter could have easily been worth a whole extra star if possible. Just the right amount of attention (my lady drinks water crazy fast, so a good key to her heart is a full water glass) and privacy. Lots of levity in the room as everyone was enjoying their dinners. Great vibe with upbeat music. 

We happened to be celebrating my birthday, which I do every year (ha!) with a fancy sushi (Nakazawa, Neta, Kura, etc.). Never done a repeat before but I'm pretty sure I'm coming back to Shuko next year.

Although the food experience was wonderful and I love the atmosphere and being there with my daughter, the reason why it didn't get a five is because when we got the bill they made such a blatant error it was as if they were hoping we would not notice they charged us $60 extra. And the way the waiter reacted to it was as if he was not that surprised, and readily changed the bill without providing a good reason for the mistake. 

My advice to others is this is a fantastic omikase menu, but please be careful and diligent in checking the bill before paying.

The best omakase ever! I really enjoyed it!
Highly recommend! Quality of fish was amazing!!! Cant wait to go back!
One of the best meals I've ever had! Everything so fresh and beautifully served. Sexy and hip atmosphere. Scallop and maitake tempura sushi were amazing! I def come back! Thank you Chef Jimmy!

Very interesting and different experience.   Went for dinner and was seated at the bar.  We were off to the side so we didn't get to have chef Nick Kim or chef Jimmy Lau prepare our food.  That was a little disappointing. That being said, the food was amazing, fresh and  delicious.  Each course was served pretty fast by Jason (our friendly cook at the corner seats) until we requested a slow down and they accomodated.  The place was busy with many regular and the large staff  (more employees than guests) seemed to know everyone yet all were enjoying the loud eclectic music. It's was different atmosphere than other Kaiseki restaurants we've been to

Great service, sake, Omakase. First time experience for sushi and they were kind enough to serve all the pieces seared (I don't eat raw). It was mouth watering and left me wishing I could eat here daily.
I've lived in NYC for 6 years, and have tried so many different foods - by far the best meal I've ever had here, nothing will ever ever compare!!!

It can be hard to get seats but I was actually able to snag one during a weekday walk in. Most of the seating is at a bar but there are two tables for larger parties. 

We got the sushi omakase and really loved every bite! Their menu changes depending on the day but we had some amazing tuna and uni. Wish we sat a bit closer to our chef so we could ask questions more easily but the vibe overall was wonderful. 

All of the staff were really friendly and helpful but also gave everyone space to have their own conversations. They also gave us a delicious slice of pie with a candle for my birthday and a card to take home! Would love to be back sometime for another amazing experience.

Surprisingly bad experience. Was up-sold the whole time. The waiter told us that because we were a few minutes late (let me stress, only a few) that we could not get the Kaiseke (175 per person). He told us we could get the baseline sushi menu (135 per person) and he would select additions from the a la carte menu. I asked if the price would be comparable to my fiance and I getting Kaiseke. He said yes. Suddenly, we get a bill for almost 600. Why? Because the additions he ordered us (that were supposed to be the same as what was on Kaiseke) cost over 200 extra! We were told to allot time for a two hour meal...we were hustled out in less than an hour. Basically we were up-sold and hustled out while two people next two us who got there around the same time were allowed by other waitstaff to get the Kaiseke.

Amazing experience.  We came here for my birthday for the $175 Sushi Kaiseki.  Made a reservation for the bar seats (highly recommended).  The pieces of sushi that we had were fresh and delicious.  Not normally picky about sushi, but you could tell why this place is so popular.  The appetizers were tasty and creative.  The grape sorbet was light and refreshing and the apple pie was probably one of the best I've had in NYC (and I love apple pie).  

I would skip on the additional supplements if you're eating the Kaiseki menu as it has more than enough food to fill you up.  

The service here was one of these I've ever had.  It took us about 2 and a half hours to finish the meal.  The water and wine glasses were never empty.  Empty plates were cleared promptly after each dish, but not in a manner where you feel like you're being rushed.  

Even though the restaurant is small, the environment was cozy enough where you could still hear your partner talk and converse with the chef or people around you if you wish.

This is a very well run establishment with fantastic food that fills you up.  Five stars all around.

I made an account just to write this review. 

This was probably one of the top 3 meals I've had in my life. My girlfriend and I tried the Omakase and had the good luck of having Chef Nick making our food for the night. The sushi was absolutely superb.  Each piece was very unique in both style and flavor. Nick noticed what we liked in the first half and catered the 2nd half of the Omakase to our tastes and even gave us each 4-5 extra pieces. After the Omakase, I was chatting with Nick and we mentioned that we were celebrating my girlfriend's birthday and they brought out a slice of apple pie with a candle in it! Our server JD ended up beautifully singing Happy Birthday in Japanese and when he finished the entire restaurant erupted into applause. Lastly, they gave her an adorable signed birthday card that said "I love the way you roll" with lots of little sushi rolls on the cover. 

5/5 Service
5/5 Sushi

I will definitely be back again

Amazing sushi - OK kaiseki.

So working backwards but starting with the positives were the sushi.  It was among the best I've ever had.  Just a small notch below sushi nakazawa.

The kaiseki however left something to be desired.  2 out of the 6 or 7 dishes were very good but everything else was a miss.  Not the worst thing in the world but it set the tone for the meal and wasn't nearly as great as the sushi.  

The other thing I didn't love were how they pushed the supplements so hard.  Big rip offs - we did two, one was blah one was great but neither worth the crazy prices.

So overall - if done right - this place is a huge win, but watch the potential pitfalls!

One of my favorite sushi restaurants! So worthy
Good service and fresh fish. The uni is soooo good

I hardly write reviews however had the most disappointing experience/sushi at Shuko. My husband and I were celebrating our 6th anniversary and were hoping to have a nice night out together. First we had requested to sit at the bar but ended up at a table and we were practically sitting on top of another couple. Second the sommelier seemed inexperienced and truthfully didn't care. I doubt they poured us our whole bottle given that the whole meal was rushed... finished the omakase in under an hour. Lastly the sushi was bland and unremarkable and the apple pie that people rave about was terrible! There is absolutely nothing special about this place. If you want quality sushi and a nice experience, try Sushi Nakazawa. Will never come back or recommend Shuko again!

A very non-traditional upscale sushi omakase experience. The head chef here worked for Masa briefly and left to open Shuko, which has one of the largest sushi counters I have ever seen. There are almost just as many staff working as there are diners too so the service here is excellent. They have a great sommelier and fantastic glassware. While the fish is good quality it is not the best and some of the combinations and seasonings are a little too fusion. Octopus was a little too chewy. That said, the rest of the food was good, fresh, tasty, and served with care. This is a great date spot or place to impress Japanese-food-"lovers" that aren't too picky about their sushi.

One word. Kaiseki. 

You probably went the extra mile with planning or leveraged the concierge service on your credit card or work to land a reservation so why not go all out for the mix experience over the straight up omakase. 

With the Kaiseki you get a mix of prepared small dishes which hot and cold plus finish off with 17 amazing pieces of sushi.  Better come hungry because it will be a lot of food in the end so be prepared to loosen the belt.  They do offer some extras as supplemental additions if you want but they give you plenty already with the Kaiseki.    

Dessert that came with the Kaiseki was pretty amazing. There was like a grape sorbet and probably one of the best apple pies I've had and i usually hate apple pie. 

Simple spot just south of usq. Only maybe 3-4 tables as the experience is catered towards eating at the sushi bar for service. We were with a large group for a birthday dinner so luckily scored a table reservation but i think shoot for the sushi bar if you can.

we celebrated our 3 year anniversary at shuko a couple of weeks ago and it was an incredible experience. the entry to this establishment is rather unassuming - you could walk right by it and never know there's an incredible restaurant residing behind its door.

we had the sushi kaiseki option and were absolutely enamored with all aspects of our meal. the kaiseki was $175 per person and included a number of composed dishes that were served first.

we were at shuko for about two glorious hours, and that would be a safe amount of time to allot yourself for the sushi kaiseki meal. i would imagine the omakase (which is $135 per person) would require a little less time. one thing that stood out to me was how attentive their service was, without being intrusive. our dinner was highlighted by our awesome seats at the counter - we were sitting right in the center and our primary chef was nick, who was such a professional and super nice! we could watch him make sushi all day.

a few of my favorites of the night were the tuna tartare with caviar and milk bread, the santa barbara uni sushi, and the scallop sushi. next time, we'll probably just do the omakase because we were so incredibly full by the end of the night.

We got the kaiseki menu and had a great experience.  Overall, I think I liked the cooked dishes more than the sushi because there was so much creativity and fun flavors (loved all the sauces), but everything was good.

1. Chawanmushi with ikura and green peas -- this was served cold, and it was a nice and refreshing opener
2. Dungeness crab with shaved cucumber -- a great summer dish; the saltiness of the crab (very good-sized portion of crab!) was balanced by the cool cucumber
3. Toro and caviar with Japanese milk bread -- simple and as good as everyone says; the bread was the perfect combination of chewy and crunchy, and toro and caviar need no further intro
4. Fluke with mushrooms and nori breadcrumbs -- this was pretty delicious; I loved the flavors, but only criticism might be the mushroom and sauce might have overpowered the fish a bit
5. Grilled sepia with heirloom tomatoes and creamy corn -- the sepia was perfectly cooked, and that corn was soo good
6. Hanger steak with nectarine and broccoli -- steak was a nice medium, and the salt of the steak and charred broccoli went well with the sweetness of the nectarine and sauce
7. Sushi tasting -- 17 pieces, including a their version of a spicy tuna roll (seared toro with fresh chili handroll...I'd eat that everyday) and another toro roll.  I appreciated that the sushi was served very simply and traditionally; just the fish with a bit of wasabi and brushed lightly with soy sauce; no fancy sauces here, and none needed.  Some unique pieces that you don't normally see were a red snapper that was lightly seared with the skin on and dorado.  My favorites of the night were probably the uni (super fresh and creamy) and the ocean trout, which I almost am ashamed to say was my favorite but it had such a strong and memorable flavor.  There was also a soft shell crab sushi, which didn't look all that pretty, but it was delicious -- lightly fried and very meaty. And last but not least, there was the toro from the collarbone (kama toro), which the chef scraped directly from the collarbone and then plated...yum.  The sushi tasting ended with a shiso leaf wrapped inside a lotus root.
8. Strawberry granita -- this was a light and refreshing dessert and a good segue into the last dessert
9. Apple pie -- I was not expecting apple pie for dessert at a Japanese restaurant, but this was one of the best apple pies I've had.  Besides the filling, I'm all about pie crust, and they had a wonderful crumble on top and a perfect crust that was neither too flaky nor felt too heavy.

Had high expectations for this dinner. Everything I expected and more. Service was knowledgeable but light hearted. Beautiful plating. Explosive flavors. One of those dinners you don't mind reaching deep in your wallet after. Bravo Nick and Jimmy!

So many previous reviews suggesting bad/rude chefs ... they must've changed chefs then.

Mine was a very pleasant younger looking chef who was excellent.

Every single piece was up there with some of the best Omakase sushi in NYC (Seki, Gari, Nakazawa, etc)

Overall most of the piece were very very good, even great but not amazing.

Finally got to one piece with jalapenos and it had a very very unique flavor. I am not a purist, I like my experiences to be with various unusual ingredients that add flavor or spice (see Seki/Gari mentioned above)... so I think that's the only thing that would've made it 5-Star for me... a little more experimentation, but truth be told I'd probably have it at 4.5 Stars.

Overall, sushi, experience, everything was excellent. And would definitely go back.

I don't know what these comments about phone use are about, I used my cellphone as needed. As did the two celeb actor dudes sitting next to us.

Had a bit of a disappointing experience here in the end. Came for my birthday dinner and did the omakase. Unfortunately, we were seated next to a very drunk single man. He disturbed our meal numerous times, tried to feed me his unwanted sushi, and was ultimately asked to leave. The staff felt bad for us and gave us a free shot, but the experience really ruined the enjoyment of our meal. And when you're paying this much money, you want it to be a great experience. I think he should have been asked to leave earlier in the meal.

As for the food, I thought the sushi was good and really liked the duck and crab apps. Some of the other dishes were less memorable. Overall, I wasn't blown away and enjoyed the omakase experiences more at Nakazawa, EN Japanese Brasserie and Neta.

Probably the most talked-about Japanese restaurant in NYC this past year, so I was going in with high expectations for my anniversary dinner. We chose the Kaiseki menu,  a combination of sushi and other cooked/raw dishes that focuses on seasonal ingredients. 

We started off with crisps topped with a refreshing seafood salad, followed by a delicious poached lobster in buttery broth. Then a golden bowl of tuna tartare with an equally-sized mound of caviar, eaten with homemade milk bread (lightly toasted and barely sweet like the Asian bakery breads I love!). There were raw scallops under a mound of crisp vegetables, as well as a surprisingly well-prepared hanger steak with a perfect sear, over an earthy roasted pepper puree and delicate sweet snow peas. Needless to say, after these first 5 courses I was pretty full. And then there was sushi.

We had about 15 pieces of sushi and a handroll, but unfortunately we were not with one of the 2 main sushi chefs. The fish is undoubtedly high-quality, but the knife skills of our chef were lacking (1 main chef asked ours to re-do some slices). Some pieces were too thick or uneven, and (very oddly) our chef pre-sliced our fish and put them into a cooler until we were ready (whereas the main chef sliced to order and his pieces appeared more uniform). I'm being picky here but considering the many (MANY) omakase options in NYC, the standards have been set high. Our chef did kindly offer to use less rice if we were getting too full. 

Dessert included a palate-cleansing sorbet, and (to my delight) a slice of warm apple pie with bay leaf ice cream. It was a spectacular dessert, and something entirely unexpected at a Japanese restaurant. I polished it off despite my seriously full stomach. 

Service was friendly, water glasses were never empty. One of the master chefs was chatting openly with his diners, and I was definitely jealous of that interaction (similar to Nakazawa) which elevates the entire experience. 

Overall, I would definitely recommend Shuko, especially for the value (a very filling and satisfying meal) - at $175, the kaiseki is an amazing value! If possible, call ahead to request one of the 2 main chefs and hopefully you will have a better sushi experience. By no means was the omakase portion bad, but it was simply not as good as many other omakases in the city potentially because of our chef. The fish quality though is spectacular, and the non-sushi dishes were also very very good.

The sushi was nothing short of amazing, their bourbon list was extensive and filled with wonderful Japanese and Taiwanese selections. I had Nikka miyagikyo which paired wonderfully with the meal, I used a single ice cube.... as the ice melts it opens the flavor of the liquor making it lighter and sweeter as the meal goes on. All this being said, when you come to Shuko you aren't paying for your actual sushi, you are paying for the experience, which is incredible. There is fine attention to detail at every point of the meal. It was a wonderful omakase experience. 
    On the other hand I am certain there are cheaper sushi places in the city that are just as delicious, maybe not as routed in Japanese tradition and less expensive. My only truly negative commentary is the fact that they played awful popish rap music through out my entire meal... the music did not match the ambience of the restaurant or the experience, and was loud to the point of not being able to tune it out. Cheap music in a restaurant that holds its food to the standards of which Shuko does just makes absolutely no sense. The music selection in my opinion cheapened the experience. I like to get down, but not at a restaurant that charges $135 a head at minimum.

I'm really happy my first kaiseki/omakase experience was at Shuko.

For $175 a person (kaiseki), you're served a few dishes before the sushi tasting along with some yummy dessert.

We had Jimmy Lau serve us our sushi and it was easily noticeable how much he enjoyed his job. For the first time, sushi melted in my mouth and I didn't think that was ever possible. Even though coming into Shuko was intimidating for me at first because I'm used to cheap eats, the staff really made me feel welcomed and comfortable. 

P.S. touching the wooden table feels amazing and you can find Shuko on a vice/munchies documentary if you're interested in learning more about the chefs and restaurant.
