Been here a few times now and the food is excellent.  However, last time I made a reservation I specifically made it to be seated at the bar, which is the whole point of going to an expensive omakase dinner. The experience is simply not the same at the tables.  This is an undeniable fact.  

I get a call the morning of my reservation saying they don't have bar seats available for me anymore.  This is just completely unacceptable.  I took the table option offered as an alternative anyway because we had a guest visiting and we had already been here before.  However, the experience was just not the same.  Not to mention, the table option is extremely cramped and not comfortable and you feel like you are practically sitting on top of your neighbors and can hear their every breath.   Kind of ridiculous considering how high end this place is supposed to be.  

How can you kick out people from their sushi bar reservation?  Well I'll tell you how.....we realized there was a celebrity there that night and they clearly bumped us from our spots in the celeb's favor.  So that's how they roll I guess.  Won't be back after that.

I like this place, it's kinda like a speakeasy Japanese restaurant, that the front door doesn't have any signage except a lavender hanging on the wall. When You walked right in, you could feel the secretive and hospitality of the restaurant. 

My friends and I was sat on a table and ordered the set menu (the longer option). My bad for not remembering all the dishes, because we have eaten over 20 courses! With the price of $170, Shuko was pretty generous with their options compare to other places. We had about 7 appetizers, daikon soup to clear your taste bud before the 15-20 pieces of sushi, apple pie and shaved ice for dessert!

It was an amazing experience and we were satisfied with varieties but some of the dishes could be a little repetitive.

Brought my sushi-loving fiancé here as a gift for his 30th birthday. He had just been talking about how he would love to go to Tokyo someday and eat real, authentic, Japanese sushi. A flight to Japan wasn't in my budget for his birthday gift, but Shuko was the next best thing.

When we arrived, the host informed us that the party before us had arrived late so unfortunately they would have to seat us late, but it wouldn't be more than 15 minutes. They're pretty strict about timing so I knew 15 minutes meant 15 minutes and that they weren't just stalling. We went to a bar nearby for a drink and when we came back 15 minutes later they seated us immediately.

The service was impeccable and exactly what you would expect for the price you're paying. 

Food: we ordered the Wagyu beef as an appetizer, which was amazing, and then had the 16-piece tasting menu. Everything tasted amazing, and i am not the biggest fan of sushi to begin with! The sushi chefs prepare each piece right in front of you, and place it on your plate when it's ready, so it feels like you have your own personal chef.

Overall a wonderful experience and definitely a good spot for a special occasion.
Their Drop the Mic, ocean trout, uni, and Toro were outstanding. All of the pieces in the sushi omakase were really good. Will definitely come back for more.

The sushi was excellent. The service very friendly. Limited space. almost every seat is around the sushi bar. A few small tables and supposedly a 6 person table downstairs. Pricier than some other comparable sushi omakase places.

So why is it 1 star only? because of their reservation policy
I'm fine with part 1 of policy that they would charge my card if I don't show up or cancel. That is expected for most high end restaurants. They can't be expected to take a loss because I can't keep reservation.
What I'm NOT okay with is part 2 and 3 of policy
1) If someone else comes in and takes my place, they STILL charge my card. So you want to make double profit?
2) If I'm more than 15 minutes late, they will refuse to seat and serve AND still charge card. They say because they "want to preserve the chef and dining experience". I don't care if I have a 3 hour or 3 minute meal. If you're charging my card, I expect my meal to be served.
(Yes, I was 20 min late. Friend started omakase courses. And yes, eating 4 pieces quickly was perfectly fine with me.)

Otherwise, would have been 4 stars
A stunner. The only negative to point to in Shuko is how hard it is to get a reservation .

As always, impeccable sushi and great service. The four of us was seated at the corner of the bar and enjoyed our kaiseki omakase on a Friday night. This time we did not have the additional pieces since we know we will be very full. We celebrated 3 birthdays and the amazing host decide to learn the birthday song in Chinese. He did it in 2 hours! 
They are very busy and reservations are hard to come by. They strive to know their customers with friendly and fun chefs and hosts. Highly recommend.

I have dined at Shuko twice and can say without a doubt that it is the best omakase/sushi meal I have enjoyed in the past two years since I began my NYC omakase journey. 

Shuko is just my kind of place. It's just cool. The background hip-hop jams along as you enjoy your meal, piece by piece atop the long, high bar. The sushi is soft and full of flavor. The restaurant is well lit, but with no windows, you feel like you're in a secret sushi den, purposely isolated from the busy streets outside. 

My fiancée and I have sat at both the bar and at one of the two tables. I prefer the bar, but the table is intimate and not a bad option. 

The staff are professional and able to accommodate allergies and restrictions. My fiancée has celiac and cannot eat gluten - they were more that happy to tailor her meal appropriately (I believe they had GF spy sauce. We also keep kosher - they were well prepared based on the notes I made prior in our reservation.

Props to the sake sommelier and his lapel pins. Complement him on his Mario or Luigi if he ha it on. He answered my specific questions and didn't take himself too seriously. Thanks!

The restaurant is expensive, but well worth the treat. We will be back. It is a tough reservation to get! You may need to stay up until midnight two weeks before, but you can also get alerted in the Resy app when a spot opens up.

An absolutely perfect meal! My husband and I came here for our first anniversary and could not have been treated better. The sushi was melt-in-your-mouth divine and the service was incredible. They really went above and beyond to make us feel special. Can't wait for an opportunity to visit again.

Due to unforeseen events, I was 1 hour late to my reservation and the restaurant staff was very understanding and took care of my guest while she waited. Food was divine and wine service excellent. Overall experience 5 stars! Will definitely be going back!

Food does not disappoint! But if you prefer sushi, don't order the expensive omakase. It's more cooked dishes than sushi. I was very full, but I thought I was going to have more sushi. The staff is excellent, very detailed oriented.

We had an amazing time here! Get a bar seat. The cuts of fishes were delicious while we kicked back to some Kendrink Lamar flowing over the speakers. Sake flowing. They were attentive and our glasses were always full and our table settings on point when we moved them around too much haha. 

It was a 2 hour meal of delicious. Some of our fav were the add on - wagyu beef and charcoal seared toro. So fatty. so decadent. I would've had more if I wasn't so full already from all the other nigiri.

Sake recommendations were great, we did something light and sweet and then switched it up with one that was fuller body and earthy. Perfect timing as it complimented the Hokkaido Uni that was placed in front of us.

Can't wait to come back again. Treat yourself!

My boyfriend brought me here for our one year anniversary. The restaurant is discretely hidden with no signage aside from the building number 47. You walk into a small curtain room with no idea what to expect, but then upon being greeted and directed in SIMPLICITY AND BEAUTY. The staff was beyond attentive and very respectful and friendly. Knowledgeable and recommending of food and drink options. The head Chef, The King was very engaging and delicately flawless in his work. The food was amazing. Such smooth and fresh fishes perfectly paired with minimal sauces. This is a real Japanese experience and cuisine.  The cocktails are also phenomenal along with the bartender who essentially made the rest of our night a delight with her recommendations and friendly gestures. Overall, this was the best dining experience my boyfriend and I ever had. The level of respect and culture is pleasant and refreshing. GO!

The value is really good! 
Love the food, service and the chef!
Will be one of my omakase to-go spot!

The music and combination of whatever you take a bite of, has a way of working together. I had a different experience with each piece of fish I tasted. At one point I truly relived a childhood moment because of a piece of seaweed that had just the right amount of salt to bring me back to tasting seaweed for my first time at the beach as a child. In my 23 years of living, this was the most intertwined experience between the music, authenticity, and taste. 

Also, I had tried my best to respect the culture of the environment and had the most pleasant time conversing with the chef in front of me.

Overall I really enjoyed my dinner experience at Shuko. It is not traditional Japanese restaurant and actually there was no one Japanese from chefs, servers to customers. So if you want to have really authentic and pure Japanese sushi or Kaiseki, you may be disappointed. To me, it is japanese fusion, you can feel that some of the dishes of kaiseki are actually taste more like thai and chinese. 

I ordered Sushi Kaiseki, it offered a lot of food, it was really worthy, especially you would be able to try so many different dishes, actually it is quite fun. Personally I enjoyed courses before the sushi course more. For the sushi courses, the fish was cut very generously, and they offered you quite a few different sushi courses from toro, that is nice. Especially the grilled toro with thai chili piece, that is the best to me at  that night or even among the best pieces I have ever had in my life. Generally the fish quality is good but still have some gap compared to the top sushi restaurant in the city. I read somewhere that most fish here come from spain farm. And you know for really top japanese sushi place in the city, a lot of fish comes from Japan, that might make a difference. But for the money I paid for this meal, really no complain. We all know how expensive it can be for really really top sushi place in the city, like Ichimura or something like that.

For the atmosphere, I really like it. It is fun, laid back, not boring at all. People enjoy conversation with their company without worrying disturbing anyone. Seems, everyone has good time. I have to say I love the energy here, cozy, fun and more dynamic. I do find sometimes really pure japanese sushi place is boring and too quiet  , I feel worried to make any noises.

Service is really nice. The chefs are humble, professional and friendly. The servers are quick ,polite and they know what they are doing, so you can just totally leave everything to them just enjoy. But there are so many or too many servers, or cooks, it is overwhelming. I really think some of them don't have anything to do , just standing there, or come to chefs to ask some idea about cooking. It is kind of distracting. By the way, one funny thing is that the smell, I wish the restaurant can smell more like restaurant, instead of some aisa temple.
Wow! The best Omakase I have had outside Japan.  Loved the vibe, wine list, service and of course freshness of the sushi. Can't wait to go back and try the sushi bar.
Yum, a great spot to celebrate a special occasion. They give you so much food for the kaiseki, so definitely go in with an empty stomach.

DISCRIMINATION, BEWARE
(Please take 5mins to read as it may save you $200)

As you can see, I don't usually write reviews. But SHUKO is the worst dining experience I've ever had in the states. Trust me, I've had many Omakase experiences in my life.

So me and my girlfriend were at the counter-top seating of the restaurant. About half-way through my dinner, one of the chef complained about the red light coming out of my camera (which i've used to take food pictures for the past two years). He said that sometimes it reflects from his knife to his eyes. I didn't realize that I was doing that, I apologized and I didn't do it again. I guess it was my fault.

About 15mins or so after the red light incident, my girlfriend puts her chopsticks pointing towards the area where they were working. So the same chef came to our side to serve us another sushi, and at the same time he told us that it is disrespectful to put the chopsticks that way. Towards the end of his lecture he told us something like "maybe you guys are from a different culture so it's okay". I find that sentence VERY DISCRIMINATING. If it's okay why do you emphasize on it so much? Even so, my girlfriend didn't do it on purpose and EVEN apologized! Telling us politely to move the chopstick to a different position would've sufficed. But we continued our course anyways.

And about 15mins after that, the same chef serve us another sushi. He saw us with our phone before he served it to us. Then he gave us a lecture about not to use our phone during dinners because we won't enjoy the moment and at the same time disrespectful to the chefs. I told him that he didn't have to worry about us as we are enjoying the dinner regardless we use the phone or not. Besides, I was looking for the type of fish on Google most of the time. Am I not allowed to know what I'm eating? After that he asked "where are you from?" This I feel is also DISCRIMINATION. What does it matter where we are from? It is one thing to ask that question after a friendly conversation, but it's a different thing to ask that after a disrespectful lecture. 

He embarassed me and my girlfriend THREE TIMES as he had to lecture us infront of the other customers (counter seating is very tight and we sit really close to other diners). If he really cared so much about our dining experience, why did he try so hard to ruin it?! My girlfriend had no appetite to eat after the third incident. How can a chef prioritize his comfort on creating the food more than the comfort of the customers that are paying alot of money for the experience? Unprofessionalism of the highest order.

As you know Shuko is not a cheap restaurant, we pay alot of money for the experience as well. We feel very DISCRIMINATED to say the least. So if you wish to dine here and support a restaurant that backs discrimination, then by all means.

CHEF IS RUDE, MAKES YOU LOSE THE JOY OF EATING, NEVER COMING BACK. 

I will NEVER be coming back here again because the chef is beyond-belief RUDE. He interrupted us 3 times. 

The 1st time was because my boyfriend was using the camera and he wasn't even using flash, it was just the orange light when you focus on the food which is already subtle and not that distracting honestly. And we were sitting beside the kitchen counter not even directly facing him?  

The 2nd time was when i put my chopsticks on the my sushi plate and he said it was rude to put your chopsticks facing the kitchen? I was just innocently placing my chopsticks on the plate instead of the mount and he made me feel like i just committed a crime. At first, out of respect i even apologized. But hello? Its just chopsticks placed on a plate. Get over yourself please. 

And the 3rd time, he interrupted us before serving us our food by suggesting that we shouldn't use our phone when eating because it is disrespectful to him and we won't be "enjoying the moment" and he goes on to give more unnecessary remarks. Hello? Are you my father, why is a chef lecturing me when i just want to enjoy my meal. I believe that everyone should have every right to use their phone however and whenever they want. What right does he have to dictate how to enjoy my dinner? I wasn't even using it all the time. It was truly RIDICULOUS. I have NEVER encountered something as ridiculous and preposterous as this. 

This is even my first time writing a Yelp review because this is the first time a chef spoke to us so rudely and self-righteously to me or us. What are we? In school? We pay to enjoy our food however we want, with or without using our phones. And who doesn't use their phones while eating nowadays? 

I was really enjoying my time and moment there before he kept interrupting and the last one was THE LAST STRAW. After he said that, i lost ALL my appetite and had NO MOOD to eat further. They had to throw away all my food from then on. I suggest if you REALLY want to enjoy the food in your own way, DO NOT EVER COME HERE. It is never a good idea to eat in ANGER AND trust me, you never want to. Unless you want to waste your money or worse, LOSE YOUR JOY to enjoy the food. 

Lastly, I write this from the bottom of my heart and believe me, i always try to see the best in people but what happened tonight totally shocked me and felt VICTIMIZED by a chef who has made me waste my money, time and RUIN my precious dining experience & memories for me & my boyfriend in NY.

I recently discovered this hidden gem and I cannot get enough! The service is impeccable and the food is above and beyond. I love that you sit at a long and beautiful bar and get to see how masterful all the sushi chefs are. They work clean and it shows in the quality of the sushi. Jimmy and Nick (the owners) are both there making sushi and are both super nice. Service is technically precise without being cold. The set menu takes a while to get through but time will fly by and you will be sad when it's over. I crave Shuko weekly and I can't wait to get back there again!

My new fave spot. Great crowd and amazing vibe - lively and upbeat music. Can feel a little overwhelming if you're used to something more zen for a sushi bar experience but it's definitely worth the experience. 

Food is beyond excellent.

I had to come here after watching the action bronson vice episode haha Jonah hill was there. I need to go check this place out.

My girlfriend and I both got the omakase, shared the wagyu and both added couple of sushi supplements. The magyu is perfection, Drop the mic and Kama toro are a must! They also have an incredible Japanese whiskey selection. 

The sushi is fresh as can be and the staff are on point. I live in the neighborhood so I will definitely come back and get the kaisake!
Fantastic sushi, service, and ambience. Would highly recommend to others!

This was seriously honestly the worst restaurant experience of entire life.  I liked that sitting at the sushi bar and I liked the sushi chefs. They were great.  But the sommelier and such a miserable air of pretense about her, it ruined the whole meal. 

This place is definitely for special occasions, which we were there to celebrate.  But nah... we'll never be back.  Sushi is partly about the fish and partly about the experience. Shuko failed in the execution so we couldn't enjoy ur food at all.  Don't come as a party of 4, parties of two are really all they can accommodate. But really, don't come at all.

For the price, this place is ok. You can get it much better at other sushi places for the same price

Main complaints:
- service felt transactional 
- sushi chef for the omakase barely explained anything. just puts sushi on your table and walks away
- sushi itself, roughly half of the nigiris were good, others made me think "I'm paying this much for this??" definitely a hit or miss
- weird hip hop music playing in the background. does not fit with the overall vibe
- no one even said bye or thank you as i was leaving

If you dont have any other sushi reservatoins and need a place, go here. otherwise, spend your money elsewhere for other omakases

I usually don't write reviews but my experience at Shuko was exceptional. The atmosphere was urban with a very exciting vibe. Head chef, Nick Kim handled the sushi with the precision of a surgeon, truly a joy to watch. What I enjoyed the most was the kaiseki course menu, each plate had a unique flavor, and they were placed on a beautiful ceramic plate. Another plus was the wine selection to go with the courses. The sommelier really impressed me. I was pleasantly surprised by my experience and I can't wait to go back.

If you're a fan of omakase, put Shuko at the top of your list. Shuko was the most incredible omakase experience I've had in a long time and without question, the best sushi I've had in Manhattan. 

The quality of food and service was off the charts, combined with such an incredible unique vibe not typically found in the upper echelons of fine dining, that really made a lasting impression on me. Nick, Jimmy and the staff were extremely attentive and constantly engaging everyone around the sushi bar, the staff were so in tune with the customer experience that the second your drink/plate was finished, someone spotted it and was already changing it out. The fish was extremely fresh, and I highly recommend getting the Drop the Mic (toro, uni, black caviar, gold flakes), as well as anything else from the a la carte list. 

Looking forward to going back this week!

Geezus. Just left this place, and it was everything I hoped it would be.

You might be able to argue that this is not traditional Japanese kaiseki, or traditional anything - but I feel you would be hard pressed to argue that this place is not perfectly executing some truly awesome cuisine. 

I love sushi. I booked a reservation for two at 5:30 PM, and when my partner couldn't go, I decided to go alone. I went with the omakase, and added an order of the "meat butter" wagyu and a Drop the Mic, with a couple carafes of sake. (Please do yourself a favor and order the wagyu steak add on.) I sat right in the middle of the bar, and I enjoyed every bite thoroughly. My face contorted into all kinds of ecstasy, so much so that my sushi chef commented halfway through that he could really tell I was savoring every bite. (I have a sushi face, I can't help it, I'm fine with it.) 

The service here is excellent. Like, on point refilling your class and clearing every plate within seconds excellent. While quietly mouthing the lyrics to one of the songs playing overhead, a passing server struck up a fun conversation about the album. I kept finding myself rubbing the smooth wood countertop, honestly, I told the GM that it was sexy. It is. I had an opportunity to chat briefly with the co-owner, Nick Kim, and simply complimented him on a great establishment. 

This is the kind of intimate, seriously-good-but-doesn't-take-itself-too-seriously place that I wish I could go to every weekend. You are missing out if you have an opportunity to dine here and you don't.

Shuko was quite alright but nothing distinguished itself from other great Sushi restaurants in NYC (at least in a positive way). It's hard to say they were "non-traditional" in the most literal sense, but the omakase had its own "twist" with a couple of offbeat items and techniques (crispy rice?). The fish and execution was fine for the most part, but like some have alluded to, the vibe is just not for me: feels a bit sceney, the music was too loud, service a bit inconsistent. Given the plethora of great sushi establishments in this town, this one was ok but ok is not good enough...

This is a very delayed review, but this is one of the most memorable meals I have had in NYC!  Yes, it $$$!, but we all left with the biggest smiles on our face and definitely felt like it was worth it. The service is top notch, and every bite was better than the next.  It is always fun to watch chefs treat food like a craft!

I was very pleased with my overall experience at Shuko. Since I had reserved for an early time, there were fewer people at the bar and I had ample time to talk to the chefs. I saw Chef Lau as well. He was very approachable and nice to the customers. The service was impeccable as the waiters were very attentive. They refilled water every five minutes and cleaned the table once each plate was devoured. The one thing I thought was strange about Shuko was the Pop or Rap music playing in the background. It was discordant with the experience of the meal itself, and though I could appreciate the novelty of such an experience, the unfamiliarity of the pairing underwhelmed me. I had the Omakase, which was wonderful.

This place is not an authentic Japanese, more likely an American restaurant trying to imitate. I couldn't remember any remarkable items nor anything surprising. It was just a boring meal.  

We had the Sushi Kaiseki, it was a big disappointment. Reasons:

The food:
It had nothing to do with Kaiseki. In case you don't know what is Kaiseki, google it. From my experiences, there are a few things you can enjoy when you have Kaiseki menu.

First, the presentation, each dish should be in small portion but carefully decorated and prepared. Each dish should have different composition, different colors. You can probably spend a minute or two by just looking at it.  There was no presentation at all, all dishes looked the same. Don't trust my word, look at their pictures on yelp and google kaiseki and see the differences.

Second, the ingredient should be seasonal pick and should be something special, something you will be surprised, but we did not have any of that. Just something you can eat anywhere. 

Third, serveware bored me to death.  As mentioned at the beginning, presentation is one of the most important part of a kaiseki menu. Other than the food presentation, the serveware should be a form of art, you can spend sometime to appreciate it. The food and the serve should be a great picture.  Shuko failed to provide this, all serveware looked the same. Google it, please.

Last, the sushi, for this price I would expect something unique, but their fishes was just the quality of sushi deluxe you can have at any other Japanese restaurants. Salmon, tuna, toro, ebi, mackerel...etc, very general pieces.  The worst part was, they made bad rice.  I always say this the sushi rice is the soul of a piece of sushi, good sushi rice would dance inside your mouth. Their rice had weird texture, like over cooked, dead. Requires good talents to make the rice so bad, similar to the quality you have at the cheap Japanese take out.
Also, by sitting at the bar, we would expect to see how skillful the chef would be. It has to be a skill demonstration, that's why it is recommended to sit at the bar for omakase, but sorry, we didn't see how skillful our chef was, nothing amazed us.

Services:
They have a lot of people working, they all nice. 
The problem is, like I said in the beginning, this is an American restaurant trying to imitate, they missed a few things of being authentic.  The first thing I noticed was they dragged the chairs to seat their customers. It probably ok if Shuko was not a Japanese restaurant. One of the rules at any authentic good Japan is to avoid anything that would disturb the customers enjoying their meals. Sounds of dragging chairs? Shuko has failed. There are few other things, but enough negative comments.

Other problems:
They serve wine!!!
Serving wine gives good profit to a restaurant, but it is a bad behavior for a Japanese restaurant because the sour taste of the wine will totally destroy how you going to enjoy your sushi. That's why the authentic Japanese sushi places would only serve sake, Shōchū, whisky, beer that goes well with sushi.

It was too crowded!!!
You will be very close to your date and your unknown neighbor, something you won't experience at any authentic Japanese restaurant. Again, disturbing.  Not a comfortable environment for dining. 

The flowers were terrible!!!  

To conclude, Shuko is an American restaurant trying to imitate. For this price, you have a lot choices in the area. Don't get too stress if you can't get a reservation with your date, nothing regret for. 
This is a place for people want to take pictures for social media, or trying to be fancy, or have too much money and don't know much about sushi.

can go on forever, we had impeccable service at shuko, the experience overall was amazing. loved being able to watch the chef prepare each and every bite, having it place it on my fish or hand it to me. the sushi was very fresh, the tomo was so butter and literally melted in my mouth. i will definitely be returning!

One of the best Japanese restaurants in NYC.
The food was great, the Chef who served us was very nice and the overall experience was pure joy.

Had dinner here a few nights ago and it was amazing. I opted for the $135 sushi omakase (20 pieces) and it did not disappoint. My favorites were the toro, spanish mackerel and blue fin tuna which was scraped off right in front of you. Service was excellent and I don't mind the rap music that was playing (mostly Drake). Only drawback and i agree with other yelpers, the pieces were slightly smaller than other omakase establishments. But overall a great experience and for $135 prices are competitive. I will definitely be returning.

Excellent service and great ambiance. The bar space are not too big but very clean and modern. I had Kaiseki ($175) and it starts with 7-8 different small dishes including meats and sashimi, before it turns to sushi tasting. Sushi pieces are all fresh and nice but not as great as other top sushi places except a few pieces. Overall, the experience was great.

Had an excellent experience here last night. While I walked past the resto several times and prob looked idiotic trying to find the entrance, I did appreciate it's low-key vibe. We sat at the bar and had the omakase. We had 22 pieces of sushi total. We had a second round of two cuts of the tuna. The rice was good and the temperature of the fish was perfect. Hate when the fish comes out too cold. Unlike some traditional Japanese places this place had some good upbeat music too. Our sake was a great bottle from tochigi. Child behind the bar and the servers always kept our glasses full. Service was friendly. Our sushi chef was informative and funny. Finished off with an amazing granita. Def will be back!

Charming service. Gorgeous food. Sexy ambiance. Delicious drinks. 
This restaurant makes me happy I live in NYC.

I was very confused and dissapointed by my recent dinner at Shuko. We ordered the omakase despite the fact that most reviews seem to favor the Kaiseki option, but for $135 we figured we should have a great meal. Our first impression of dinner was that the the sommelier was very standoffish. This struck me as very odd considering their wine mark ups are just short of criminal! The Soul Cycle-esque soundtrack (read Kanye West, the Weeknd, generic R&B) didn't help us get in the mood for the dining experience to come. 

As for the sushi, the fish itself was really superb, but the rice was a bit hard, became separated from the fish as you picked it up, and the pieces themselves were quite small. They were not quite the mouthful I am used to from other great NYC sushi establishments. 

As the meal came to a close and we were mentally getting ready to leave, we found ourselves waiting almost 20 minutes for a dessert course that was neither listed on the menu, nor worth any wait at all.  If the chef chooses to list "canape"- a few roasted brussel sprouts, why not list a (two stage) dessert course- granita and a (giant) slice of apple pie?? I never order dessert at restaurants and if we had known that this was part of the price, it would have effected my decision to dine there.

With all the amazing Japanese restaurants in New York, I would advise spending your hard earned cash elsewhere. If your cash is not hard earned, then give Shuko a try. Why not.

Truly among the very best restaurants in New York. The food is certainly Japanese but it departs greatly from the traditional kaiseki experience to create something very unique and special. This departure is no more apparent than with the apple pie served at the end of the kaiseki dinner, which is delicious and has absolutely nothing to do with Japanese food.

Still, the most traditional and familiar part of the meal, the sushi, is the true highlight of the experience. Though I think the kaiseki meal is a great value at only $40 more, the sushi alone is a completely satisfying, indulgent, and outstanding meal in itself. The chefs are masters, everything is precise and perfectly executed. The fish selection couldn't be better, and you'll get seasonal offerings that aren't found too many places (shirako...with white truffle).

The service isn't quite up to par with other restaurants at this price point, but nothing to complain too much about.

Atmosphere and ambience are fine and fitting for this sort of restaurant. If you don't like hip-hop though you're out of luck.

Had a good time with my friends. The crowd will be a little stuffy so don't expect to receive laughing and joking with open arms. Like I give two shits. 

These dudes know what they're doing on the sushi tip; fuckin pricey but you go to these places with fancy guts you should expect to pay. 

I liked the music choice. I faintly remember Jay Z shit playing. Makes it more relaxed mood than the patrons, who are sitting on 3 inch circumferenced wood dowels. 

David Chang was there with some food groupie, that should mean something to you hypebeasts out there.

I love this place!  Great omakase!  One of my favorite 'date-spots'. Relaxed atmosphere, friendly staff, music selection is usually hip-hop.  Downsides: really expensive, and the music is too loud, like kind of hard to have a conversation loud.

My #1 NYC fine dining restaurant, without a doubt. Must make a reservation in advance. My favorite parts were the wagyu beef with mushrooms dish, and watching them scrape toro off a large tuna bone, put it in a piece of seaweed, and hand it to you for direct consumption. I came with coworkers, and we unanimously agree it was a wonderful experience. Definitely get the kaiseki menu.

We ordered the $175 complete prefixes. It started with cooked dishes then followed with sushi. I have to say in general I'm not impressed. The food were all good just not special enough.  The only exceptions were veal cheek, Santa Barbara uni (very sweet I like ) and charcoaled toro kama (special order). And I also particularly loved the cocktail made with Chinese baijiu that had a unique complex aroma.  But very strong. Don't think I'll come back though as there are so many excellent sushi restaurants in NYC.

Ever since I have dined at Neta, I started to count on days until my reservation at Shuko, which was opened by the same duo chef, apprentices of that famous Masa. Have had many experiences at traditional sushi, I was indeed looking forward to something different, as Lau and Kim would like to introduce upon.

Shuai offered a bit of flexibilities by introducing both the sushi Omakase and Kaiseki menu. I would recommend getting the latter, with a slight premium, you would be able to enjoy some of the better kitchen-cooked items.

I would not go through the entire menu; yet many courses have caught my heart completely. How was it possible to have that slices of octopus cooked so tender and chewy? That small piece of jige was newly introduced to NY, as that was one of the specialties in Japan. The whole sushi experiences were nothing but unforgettable! Flawless!

Aside from the regular tasting mint, Shuko certainly offered many add-on items - if you are hungry enough, or would like to have a more rounded dining experience, go for it!

Have dined at many top-notch sushi bars in the city, I would say that Shuko was definitely among tops on the list. While having a slight modern tilt, sushi at Shuko has its own unique characteristic, thanks to the help of those modern cooking techniques. I would be more than happy to pay an extra visit, just for their uni add-on piece...or shall I also go for that huge spicy crab?

Friendly reminder - you will be left remarkably full after the whole dinner, trust me, it was well worth it!

Not a traditional sushi place. It's fusion. Some interesting attempts. Some didn't work out so well. Was not what we were looking for.  The "sushi" is grossly over rated. Not Japanese. I spoke to our chef in Japanese, he shook his head and asked what I said in English because he was Chinese. It's a decent meal if you are looking for non traditional. Service was OK.  Over priced for what it is. I won't be going back.

Shuko is a phenomenal restaurant and I frequently return usually at least once every season. It has long been my favorite sushi restaurant and I cannot recommend it enough.

I always go with the kaiseki omakase. At an extra $40 versus the sushi omakase, it comes with a sequence of half a dozen or more small plates comprising both cooked and raw dishes with only a slightly truncated sushi menu. The dishes are phenomenal. Some are repeat signatures that I have had many times, others are seasonally dependent. Repeats that I always love include the toro and caviar with japanese milk toast and crispy trout skin with spicy maitake mushrooms and salmon roe. The grilled octopus, sunchokes and cauliflower cream was a stand out among the seasonals as was the roasted duck with the fried potato gratin. As a supplemental I also had the miyazaki wagyu which they jokingly call meat butter. It is worth every penny.

The sushi rounds were amazing as well. The opener is always the toro which melts in your mouth. Other stand out pieces include the supplemental drop the mic (a combination of diced toro, uni and caviar with gold flakes) and the kama toro (which is seared with white hot charcoal for an almost beef like finish). The baby shrimp which is one of the seasonal sushi was great as was the unagi which they served with a perfectly crisp cucumber rather than rice. The toro sinew with thai bird chilies also remains a perennial favorite.

Shuko is a must for any lover of sushi in the city.

Went with the kaiseki menu;  had many interesting dishes (fav was prob the strip steak) followed by the sushi portion (about 17 pieces, with a few extras thrown in).  Would consider it a special occasion type of place since the price/value ratio could have been better.     Music was not too loud, patrons were pretty laid back, chefs were engaging, service was good.    Despite what others have wrote I was not stuffed at the end, just ok.

New York's Greenwich Village's Shuko. Kaiseki with Wagyu beef side course. This place mastered both, traditional and contemporary cooking methods while still adhering to its roots: think of a Geisha who although applies contemporary makeup but is still able to recite poetry and play the classical instruments beautifully. Their ingredients are of the utmost freshness and their grasp and conveyance of the ingredients' textures are spot on: the toro and Wagyu beef melts in your mouth in waves of buttery fatty satisfaction. The vegetables are slightly crunchy yet, al-dente soft. The sushi rice are warm and tightly compact: when you pick it up with chopsticks the rice never falls apart (difficult feat). This place sent me to cloud 9 and caused a smile on my face as if I am high throughout. The service here is second to none.

NYT 3*

2nd visit, and left even more impressed with the kaiseki tasting menu tonight.
Go w/ the kaiseki, instead of the sushi omakase; For extra $40, you are getting many wonderful, some quite unique, non-nigiri dishes.

Also, got to try couple of excellent wine from Italy that paired very well w/ some of the dishes.

A treat tonight to have Executive Chef Lau prepare all the nigiri.

Impeccable service.

Highest recommendation.

: 10 calendars

I'm not sure what else anyone would want when going for sushi but this place is exceptional. 

The Sushi which is all we ate was as good as gets, the rice perfectly seasoned and medium sized pieces which to me is just right when eating sushi. They advise in the beginning eating sushi with your hands, bring a towel to clean your hands as you eat and we're highly attentive. You have your own chef right in front of you who couldn't have been nicer and more engaging if he tried. 

I've been to some of the other newer places and older ones that charge 50-100% more for essentially the same experience. I see no reason to go back after coming here. You're not going to get a better meal, experience or service anywhere else. Save the money and come here twice instead. 

The friend I went with who is a far bigger expert at Sushi agreed. 

Exceptional food, great space, good music (not too loud), comfortable atmosphere, personal attention from the chef and spot on service and all for 50-100% less then the competition.

We couldn't find any holes in this places game and we looked. Go and enjoy. Your belly will say thank you.

Came here on a Saturday night for the Kaiseki option. By far one of the best Kaiseki seatings we have ever had between or experiences in Miami and Tokyo. Though they are not entirely traditional, I loved the innovative take on their dishes. The atmosphere, staff and meal- all phenomenal. Derek was our main chef with Andrew and they were wonderful! If you get a reservation here, I'd say opt for the pricier Kaiseki, loosen your belts and enjoy the meal!
Great food. Great atmosphere. Staff was amazing. I highly recommend this restaurant for fun with friends or a special occasion.

Is it me or does no one realize HOW SMALL the pieces of sushi at Shuko are?? After dining at multiple omakase restaurants in the city, none serve such small, bland pieces at such high prices. At Shuko, none of the 14-16 pieces of sushi were memorable. It's mind boggling to me this place has great reviews. I felt rushed out the door after ordering the $135 omakase, as if they were punishing me for not spending more for other option. Depsite being half empty ( I now understand why) I was placed in a corner, while my sushi chef was half down the bar. To top it all after drinks my bill was about $500, but I was not offered a piece of apple pie, YES APPLE PIE AT A JAPANESE RESTAURANT. Speaks wonders about Shuko that the best thing looked to be the apple pie, but I wouldn't know. Anyone who has given Shuko a high rating clearly has not enjoyed a great omakase somewhere else. The most memorable part of a $500 dollar meal should not be the music.

This is the most overpriced overrated restaurant I have ever been to. I've been to numerous omakases across NYC all with far better quality fish and specifically rice. The pieces were extremely small and the add on dishes were outrageously expensive. 

In addition to the food being of mediocre quality, the service was worse. It was my birthday and my boyfriend requested them to sing or being a candle. They did nothing and brought the check. In order to make up for it, they didn't even take anything off the bill. I would recommend many other places before going to this restaurant.

I've been to many venerable sushi places and I've never felt the need to add to their praises. I had the kaiseki at Shuko. I'd rate the food 4 stars. There were some unforgettable pieces (the toro sinew and rib meat, the uni, shiso & lotus root, spicy tuna, wagyu beef supplement) but the service elevates it to 5 stars. 

This is not a temple-of-the-sushi-chef place. It's a place where you can enjoy mind-blowing sushi while kicking back with your besties to a great soundtrack. The casual atmosphere and friendliness of this staff--from Jimmy Lau, et al. to the dude who greets you at the door--sets this place apart. If I lived in the neighborhood, I'd go to Shuko all the time. 

Why the snub, Michelin?
Best  omakase  yet.  Highlights tuna tartar   with Caviar. Shrimp tempura with succotash sushi flight exceptional.  Love the horseshoe  sushi bar. Service exceptional.

The only reason I am not giving five stars is the way the meal started. We had a 5:30 reservation requiring us to wait outside dripping sweat until exactly 5:30. As soon as the doors opened, my senses were confused by the mixture of incense and sweat reminiscent of a yoga studio and the familiar cold woody scent of a good sushi bar. The space is more than a usual Omakase experience, but in a pleasant way. No one looks Japanese but it's also not bothersome. My main disappointments were the first two courses--which were not pieces. They were thoughtful, but tried too hard, with too many parts. Thankfully afterwards, there were plenty of pieces and I basically enjoyed all of them--they were pleasantly unique enough that I felt each piece was special. You will definitely have to prepare yourself for the price tag--especially if you are like me and you enjoy something to sip on (great selection for this and knowledgeable staff) and tend to have an extra piece on top to finish off the meal. Overall a lovely experience.

Interesting experience if you like or at least want to try American fusion cuisine that is inspired by sushi. The chefs at Shuko are not trying to be another japanese sushiya and they are not shy about that as demonstrated by by playing american bar music and serving different courses with totally no regard of japanese traditions (toro was the first sushi piece that was given to me, for example). 

Fish cut was generous and quality is not bad, but overall it is not close to what true sushi should be. So dont even expect that. Fish easily comes off rice and the two dont feel like an integral part at all. Some interesting tries with non-traditional sauces/pairing. (Some pieces are really, really spicy).

We got the Sushi Kaiseki and it was amazing. Definitely come hungry because it's a lot of food. Jewel Baku has been my standard so far in NYC for best sushi, but Shuko exceeded all of my expectations. The only negative I would say is that the wines are pretty expensive, so that can run the bill up pretty quickly. We sat at the sushi bar and the chef was amazing, walking us through the dishes and making us special hand rolls when we said we liked things spicy. The fish were very fresh and the toro was the perfect end note. Highly recommend!

Appropriately named "drop the mic" ... Devouring jaw dropping trifecta of #uni (from #Osaka), #toro (scraped off the bones), and #caviar (topped off with gold flakes) was an amazing experience @shukonyc.  Eaten separately was already overwhelming.  Loved the intimate space, hip hop music, and most of all the great great sushi #omakase!
The sushi omakase is one of the best I've ever had in New York, some sushi pieces taste sooooo good, that I can see fireworks in my head when I put them in my mouth :D

Good but after spending hundreds of dollars, I had to go across the street to get some pizza to fill me up(they use a hunk of apple pie at Shuko to fill you at the end but wasn't in the mood for sweet yet). My wife was full though so maybe I just have a big appetite. My standard "regular place" order would be 2 make rolls and 4 pieces and I'm stuffed. For the money, I rather sit at a nice table and have service at a real top french or italian restaurant and do the local sushi when I need my fix.....to spend 10 times the amount at Shuko it would have to be 10 times better and since my local is Sushi of Gari, it's not!!

Just got back from a two week trip to Japan where we ate at a half dozen michelin starred sushi restaurants. This place is definitely worth a trip if you can sit in Darry's section. As with all omakase experiences, I recommend sitting at the bar rather than at a table.

I've been dying to come here ever since I saw this old Vice mini sushi episode on Shuko.  Finally came here with my boyfriend for my bday dinner yesterday and sat at the far end of the counter.  This is probably my new favorite omakase spot (and i LOVED 15 East last year and didn't think anything could beat that).  Shuko was overall just my type of place from the service (wait staff, sushi chefs, and mixologists) being on point and super friendly, the food/sushi pretty much loved and was wowed by every piece, apple pie for dessert (i hate sweets but i LOVE pies), and the background of hip hop and r&b bumpin at light volumes in the background.  It was a pretty epic meal overall.  

I feel like the value of everything we got was also great.  We both ordered the sushi omakase ($135 pp) and that was for 20 bomb ass pieces of sushi as well as an amouse and this awesome crab salad starter.  We were over ambitious and ordered a supplemental ribeye and their epic drop the mic piece (uni, cavier, and like negi toro).  We were so stuffed by the end of the that we were even struggling on the last two pieces of sushi but it was so goooood.

And I have to give a shout out to the apple pie.  As mentioned before I dont like sweets in general but this pie with the burnt bayleaf ice cream was a great combo.  And yes obvi this is not a traditional japanese dessert but this isn't a traditional japanese sushi omakase place.  So that should manage your expectations.

All in all this place is bomb and my new goal is to become a regular here.  We sat next to a group of regulars and they def got some pretty sweet treatment and was serenaded by the waiter with an opera version of happy birthday.  it was pretty good.

Avg sushi and they rip you off big time if you order extra after the set menu. $20 for one piece of Uni, $25 for one mediocre seared fatty tuna.  I would rather they charge more for the Omakase and include extra 2 -3 pcs.   Definitely not in the same league as sushi ichimura or even sushi yasuda.

ARGHHH!!!!!!! I wish had taken photos of this SPECTACULAR experience. These chefs Nick Kim and Jimmy Lau are absolutely brilliant! If you have the cash to spend and are able to get a reservation..  DO IT! Best sushi quality I have EVER had and hands down the tastiest, also the most melt in your mouth Wagyu beef ever!! 
With extremely simple and ever-so elegant flavors and presentation this was a meal I will never forget!

My brother & I tried this place 2 or 3 days ago for dinner, and at the time I did not know much about the restaurant except the fact that it is a Japanese style restaurant. Usually, I study up on the restaurant before I go, but due to my busy work schedule, this time I simply showed up without learning much about the place. Since I tend to avoid raw fish, I imagined that there will be always something else cooked that I can order on the menu. And then, to my surprise, I realized it is a several course long tasting menu w/ plenty of raw fish! It seemed absurd to go through a full tasting menu and then ask to have sushi-grade fish cooked! When I was explaining this dilemma to the server, he offered to have some dishes seared instead. Honestly, with these changes/substitutions, I did not have a high expectation given my own constraints. But to my surprise, each dish was truly creative, exquisite, and incredibly delicious. I've been to many famous Japanese restaurants in various cities both in & outside of the US, but I must say this was indeed one of the best. In addition, the ambiance was elegant & chic; service was impeccable. The dinner was easily 2 hour long, and it was such an incredible dining experience, especially since the food was simply beyond-perfect. Exec Chef & owner Nick Kim came by our table to say hello. I thought he came to see this odd Asian lady who came to his restaurant not wanting to eat raw fish... :) In any case, that evening I informed one of my old college friend about this dining experience and how I'd love to go back there again. Needless to say, we already made a reservation to have a dinner there next week Wed!

I took my fiancé here for his birthday. We had the sushi omakase (sans cooked food/kaiseki) at the bar, and enjoyed every bite of our meal. We loved how creative the omakase was. I feel like their style is kind of similar to Nakazawa (flavor pairings to enhance each piece). So if you enjoyed Nakazawa, I'd definitely recommend trying Shuko's omakase. We actually thought the pieces were super small, much smaller than the usual omakase pieces, but to our surprise we were very full at the end. Our server was also kind enough to offer us a complimentary dessert.

So thankful they kindly waived the reservation charge for my friend who got ill and couldn't make it. Enjoyed the sushi omakase, but was a little let down that they served Santa Barbara uni (even though it was delicious)...was kinda hoping to indulge in Hokkaido uni. Added the special uni/caviar/toro piece but wasn't blown away. Selection of sushi was yummy and fresh. Service was very attentive. The chef was kind and introduced himself at the end and we did a fist bump, which I observed regular customers do when they come in. If only I could be a regular!!

Great sushi experience from the front door to the music to the service to the food.  Get your check book out or better yet have a friend take you.   Like enjoying a concert and it keeps getting better.   You have two choices and you can't go wrong with either.  Highly recommended

Shuko is one of the best sushi restaurants I've been to! It was my first time at a sushi bar (I usually sit at the regular tables at sushi restaurants), so it was reassuring when the chef was able to walk me through each step and introduce each fish to me. The fish were very fresh and the toro (tuna belly) is definitely a favorite! The ratio between the fish, rice, wasabi, soy sauce, and toppings was perfect, and I was really able to taste the difference between each fish. They also paired the sushi tasting with a special sake (flowery one) which was phenomenal! 
The service was great too and our waiter was so good at checking up on us and making sure that everything was going well. The atmosphere was great and I didn't have to talk over loud music or people. 
All in all, it was a great time of amazing food and service!

I made a reservation for 5:30 pm with my friend, and it was a good choice. There was only one other group there and we were seated in front of Chef Nick. I noticed as soon as I walked in the door that the workers are so nice! Our server was great. It was my first time at a sushi bar, so he walked us through the steps of ordering the food to sushi etiquette. My friend and I ordered the Kaiseki with some sake on the side. The dishes and sushi were delicious! We got started on a mochi dish, and apparently they make the mochi themselves. We also got a lobster dish from the supplemental menu, which was very spicy but also delicious. The sushi was GOOD. Although you get about 1-2 pieces at a time, the number builds up and eventually my friend and I were stuffed. It was a cool experience getting to watch Chef Nick make all the sushi in front of us. I noticed that on the Yelp reviews, some people complained that they used too much soy sauce. I actually enjoyed the soy sauce and thought that it added a nice flavor to the whole piece. I'm not sure which pieces I ate, but the toro at the beginning was so good. I normally do not like tuna, but that tuna belly is worth eating. All in all, it was a good experience with delicious food, helpful workers, and a fun environment. Chef Nick was funny and nice, always telling us what we were eating and answering our questions about the sushi. It has a high price tag, but sometimes, a price must be paid for high quality food.

Yeeeees.
Excellent excellent food.
Kaiseki recommended, worth th $40 difference.
You get savory dishes from th kitchen not the bar that is super tasty.
The sushi itself is (of course) delicious. Toro was my fav. Oh. And the seaweed "taco" soooooo good!
Alcohol paring is very generous. You.ll feel tipsy when you hop off the stool.
Cheers!

I went to one of the best New Age Japanese restaurants in Tokyo tonight -- on 12th between University and Broadway. In Greenwich Village. Some chefs honor their predecessors. Some chefs recreate.  Some reinvent. Then there's Nick Kim and Jimmy Lau. They start with the ingredients that we all long for, and just create a new level of cuisine. Shuko goes up like a rocket and never comes down.  And to be on that ride is one of best dining experiences in New York. And Tokyo.

My heart is broken! I wanted to love this place for so long and our meal was totally ruined. The service was aloof and miserable. I can't even imagine why we were treated so poorly but $650 later (two tasting menus, a wine pairing, a few beers, tax and tip) I wish I never set foot here.

Let's talk about the price because $185pp is insane for dinner. I'm not cheap and many tasting menus are worth the price. I thought Shuko would be an amazing experience but it was totally basic and at times, uncomfortable. The sushi was OK and the muscular, tattooed sushi chef was super cool and talkative. But other than that, the service left me feeling like I just wanted to leave.  

This place ruined my birthday and weirdly, I haven't ordered sushi since. I wish I never went.

No thoughts whatsoever put in to the course. They must have bribed Peter Wells, the food columnist at New York Times, to give them a good review. This place is absolutely rubbish. Uni was from a package and thickness of every single sushi was different. $175 price tag for this disaster is a joke. And don't fucking call it Kaiseki.

I tried this place after reading a good review from the NYT. But what a ripoff! I thought Le Bernardin was at the apex of the ripoff in restaurant business, but I was wrong. Shuko is probably one of the worst food deal you can find in NYC. It is simply expensive Benihana. They sell "Kaiseki"menu, but what they are selling is disgrace to real Kaiseki cuisine. Every single one of their dishes was unimpressive and tasteless. Their soy sauce lacked flavor, too salty, and sushi was not fresh or tasty. If you are paying $175 for a course, you expect something remarkable, not the quality of sushi from suburb Asian fusion restaurant run by Chinese (no offense for Chinese people running Japanese restaurant but it is typically a bad sign). There was no philosophy or harmony in the entire course. An apple pie (really. F**king apple pie.) at the end of the course was a final blow. I really want my money back! What do you call this, a food robbery?

Had the sushi omakase that supposedly came with 2 dessert, but they forgot to give me the apple pie and gave me the check instead. So I paid and left. The service is horrible. For the price, this place feels like a ripoff. The food itself is basically the same as Neta. I would have gone to Neta and got pretty much the same kind of sushi and pay less without any of the crappy service. There was only 20 of us and wasn't even a full house. It's like going to china town and eating at an empty cantonese noodle place where the waiter forget to refill your water. Seriously, charging this much for such a crappy service should be made illegal.
Went here for my birthday and had a great time.  The food was delicious.  I enjoyed each and every course.  The service was excellent.  I dont think I've ever had better service.

My wife and I arrived in New York to a drizzly, traffic snarled morass that scotched our cocktail plans with friends; it was up to Shuko to save the day. There was a bit of a wait (this is a tiny space) but the delightful British lady at the door helped while away the time with fun chat. Suddenly, it was time to sit at the beautiful bar and begin our omekase meal (we were starving after a long day of travel). Our sushi chef was silent but friendly (he was not one of the owners) and began to carefully form the delicious torrent of sushi creations that were to follow for the next hour. My lovely wife selected the Marisa Cuomo Furor, a crisp white from Amalfi (folks who know a thing or two about pairing wine with seafood I suspect). I am foggy on the details of the myriad of rolls and other treats we enjoyed since I am writing this nearly a week and several great meals after the fact, but suffice it to say this was the best sushi experience I have had in 35 years of raw fish revelry. The two different mackerel rolls stood out, one dusted with yuzu zest as did enoki mushroom "salad" in kewpie mayo on a toasted rice cake. The pear gratine' was perfect clean finish to a superb meal. Next time, Keisuke!!

Came here for my birthday, loved the kaiseki sushi omakase!  They ask you if you have dietary restrictions or anything you strongly dislike - I did let them know I strongly dislike fluke, so they did not serve me any of that.  Where I went wrong was that I only thought about fish, forgetting that this was kaiseki on top of a sushi tasting!  They served me lamb which was completely unexpected, I didn't enjoy that because I'm not a fan of lamb but my husband ate it and liked it just fine.  I would say everything was absolutely delicious with one exception - the dessert.  They really need to up their game on this one, they served a very limp looking apple pie with ice cream on the side.  It also felt very out of place for the meal.  Hopefully they have different desserts each night.  I'll say the granita as a palate cleanser right before the apple pie - awesome!  I could have ended my night with the granita.
All I have to say is wow! The omakase was unbelievable from the first piece to the last. The pieces got better and better. So freaking yummy!!! Will definitely go back.

Shuko proves (once again) that passionate chefs + fresh ingredients = an unmatchable dining experience. Each bite was lovingly prepared, the service was impeccable, the ambiance cozy. No pretension, just the finest sushi you may ever eat (and apple pie for dessert!). Get here.
What an incredible experience! If you want to splurge for a special occasion you will not regret it. If you are a sushi lover/foodie the price is definitely worth the eating experience.

Worth every cent! It was the most memorable sushi experience I've had. The fish was sweet and tender - staff was incredibly attentive and the space is small -intimate. I highly recommend it and look forward to returning soon!

If you like sushi, come here. If you hate sushi, come here.. it will change your perspective on sushi. The kaiseki delivers a non traditional omakase that gives a fusion to seasonal ingredients that are very delicious. There wasn't a single dish or piece of food that I was unhappy with. I've been to a variety of top rated and Michelin rated sushi joints (Yasuda, 15 East, Gari, ENjb) and I put Shuko at the top of my list. The cocktail with the amaretto and green tea was solid and the selection of wine is outstanding. I'll be back...

Very good.  Very good vibe.  Enjoyed the rap music with my uni.  I also added the toro tartar and  wagyu to my sushi Omakase for me and my beautiful wife.  

The toro tartar was great but miniscule and 48 dollars.  Wagyu small but rich in flavor and worth it.   Sushi fresh and excellent but pieces small. I prefer the healthier sized slices of yasuda which are nearly double the size.  

Overall very good.  Would come back but at 700 bucks for two with drinks a bit pricy.  Wife loved it and she is hot as hell so sure we be back.

Best sushi experience I've ever had. 

I live in LA and have visited Tokyo more than once, so I know good sushi. This sushi is fantastic. The quality of the fish is top notch. Service is relaxed but so friendly and professional. 

I opted for the sushi Omakase at $135. It's really a steal for the food you get. Each bite was more impressive than the last. Flavors exploded in my mouth. Of note were the toro roll and the lobster supplement. Wine list is excellent. 

Rap music makes the atmosphere light and fun even though the food is serious.

Apple pie is a must for dessert. I cannot wait to go back!

This is our favorite Japanese restaurant offering kaiseki. It is nothing short of AMAZING. Since it's opening, we've been back 3x and we don't plan on stopping there. We've since made friends with Chef Jimmy and Chef Nick - this could be dangerous!

Food -
We always splurge and get the $175 tasting menu and we've never left unsatisfied. The mix of cooked dishes along with the nigiri...mmmmmm perfection - you cannot go wrong. The pieces are all equally delicious, however the pieces that stick out the most are...

- A5 Wagyu - melt in your mouth
- Scallop Private Parts - both female and male (yup, I am soon giving birth to a scallop). I wouldn't say it was the best thing I've ever had, but definitely the first time I've ever tried it. Would I ever eat it again? Sure, why not.
- O-toro - the waitstaff brings the chef a piece of burning charcoal to which he uses it to lightly smoke the top of the fish. Yummy!

Everything else is equally as delicious. No soy sauce needed. Make sure you use your fingers (put that damp napkin sticking up to good use!).

Ambiance -
The chefs are beyond friendly!! They will let you know exactly what you are eating, but I only pay attention half the time because I'm so eager to eat it right away - 0 patience from my end. The hip hop/pop music playing in the background makes it feel young and hip as you're sitting around the 20 seater chef's table enjoying the best meal of your life. There is also a dining alcove that seats a 2 top and a 6 top. There is also a private room downstairs. But I would prefer not to sit anywhere than in front of the chefs! Definitely a must-try and a must-return!!
Just fantastic. My wife and I ate at Shuko last night. It was my second time and her first. John David (waiter) and Wei (sushi chef) took great care of us. Overall, a glorious evening.

My first time at Shuko was a good experience. However, the second time was not so good. I was seated at the private dining area which looks like a cave. It was way too small and just not enough space for a party of 6. The third and final time I visited Shuko, I was notified 40 minutes prior to my reservation that I would be seated at the counter because my table reservation was cancelled and my reservation was delayed 30 minutes. This was an important business dinner and I had to contact my clients on such a short notice, which was very embarrassing. That is very unprofessional and no way to run a business. With that being said, I will not be returning to Shuko.

My daughter and I finally got a reservation for dinner, and were greeted warmly at the door. We were seated at the end of the counter, not the star seating, but with congenial servers and nice neighbors. Both of us ordered the Kaiseki, and after consultation some delicious cocktails to start. 
Much has been said about the excellence of the sushi, which indeed was great quality and imaginative. We felt the hot courses preceding the sushi were equally special. Very seasonal, beautifully cooked, appealingly presented. We aren't the sushi experts of some of the other Yelp reviewers, but we have spent time in Japan, eaten at Tsukiji market and private clubs in Tokyo, and experienced different styles and foods in the different regions of Japan. Our sushi chef--usually referred to as the grumpy one--was phenomenal. We didn't need the fist bumping and other shtick that some chefs rely on, what we appreciated was his expertise enhanced by his authentic warmth. 
For us this was an integrated aesthetic experience, with the food, the servers, the sushi chef, and the handpicked tableware all contributing to a wonderful night. Expensive of course, but so special compared to other places like this in NYC.

Kaiseki was SO MUCH food. I wish I had more room for sushi because that was the best part of the meal. 
Hot food was ok nothing too memorable but the Toros!! Yum. The chef came out and seared them toro and I probably had like 5 pieces myself. All other fishes were fresh and the amount of rice was perfect for the sushi. They paired a cocktail, sake and wine for us and everything was excellent. 
Come hungry!

The great thing about New York is that there's a never ending stream of great sushi spots that constantly open up. I've been wanting to come to Shuko since it opened to the point where I was afraid my expectations were too high.

I got the $135 menu and it was probably one of the more creative omakase's I've had (similar to what they do at Gari). Each piece had its own twist - although they had the classic toro, uni and scallop. 

In all I would say we had around 20 pieces, but fear not! I was pretty intimidated that I would be stuffed walking out, but the chefs do a great job of balancing the rice to fish ratio and I didn't feel like I was being force fed rice like I am at some places.

And as with any sushi place - definitely try to sit at the counter instead of a table.

We chose to do the kaiseki meal which was, to be honest, way too overwhelming. It started with hot dishes and ended with sushi. I think it makes more sense to start with the sushi since its taste is much more delicate. By the time we got to the sushi dishes we were almost full and so couldn't enjoy the freshness of the fish as much. 

The hot dishes were good but not great unfortunately. And for the price point and the hype that Shuko gets, I was really expecting to have my mind blown with each dish. All the hot dishes were average and it felt like each dish was "trying too hard". My favorite was the wagyu add on - simple yet wonderful - the meat was super tender and juicy and only seasoned with some sea salt. 

The sushi part of the meal was quite good! If I come back next time, I'd stick to the sushi meal. Also make sure you sit at the sushi bar to get the better experience.

:: A foodgasmic sushi omakase with a twist ::


Reservation needed? YES!! I made one a month out. I would also request on the phone to sit with either Jimmy or Nick, the two head chefs

| Food |

- We tried the $135 sushi omakase with the addition order of seared Wagyu beef. I knew I was in for a spectacular sushi feast when the first piece of sushi that landed in front of me was Toro. We were fortunate to have Jimmy, one of the co-owners, serve us and I loved the way he prepared every single piece. All the pieces were traditional with a slight twist to it that bring out or compliment the fish that it is served with. For example, my favorite toro chopped scallion roll had ginger wrapped up inside. Each piece was so unique and it's funny to say that the most "boring" of them all was that first piece of Toro! My favorite 12 pieces were (see collage):

1. Uni Toro Caviar with gold flakes roll
2. Toro Scallion roll
3. Hokkaido Uni
4. Ocean Trout with Jalapeno
5. Chill Toro Sinew
6. Soft Shell Crab
7. Maguro tuna with garlic
8. Sea Bream with shiso pickled plum
9. Spicy Ocean Trout
10. Spring onion and mushroom over crispy rice
11. Shiso with pickled lotus root
12. Kampachi with spicy potato

The meal ended perfectly, but nontraditional for a Japanese restaurant, with apple pie  and ice cream. The apple pie had a special flavor and I found out it came from miso which  isadded to the dough to help with umami. Arigato Jimmy! Still thinking about this meal and can't wait to visit again!

| Ambiance |

-The ambiance is louder than that of most traditional sushi bars which I liked because it felt more relaxed and comfortable. Sometimes it can be intimidating eating at the sushi bar with the sushi chef staring at you while you eat each piece, but Jimmy made us feel right at ease and joked around with us too while we ate :).

Friend invited me to check out the new spot, as she loves to try all Omakase (mainly in NYC and SF). She's lived in Tokyo for extended periods twice. Jimmy served us directly, and the meal was outstanding. Every bite was superb starting with a Mochi like i had never had. Wagu followed closely as an add on ($50 we split and was melt in your mouth) I believe after a sea bream dish. Then approx 20 pieces of stunning yet very diverse sushi. 

Amazing service, and wonderful host who sat us on request at the left end of the bar (I walked in early fully affected by that day's humidity and asked to be out of the way). 

Thank you to everyone on staff. Wonderful meal and experience. The Kaiseki looked excellent, but we are more purists. Maybe next time. Looking forward to a return.

This meal was soooooo good. I've been wanting to go here ever since I moved to the neighborhood, and everything still exceeded my expectations. The entire restaurant wraps around the sushi bar which makes a perfect setting to watch the chefs make the most delicious food. 

The sushi portion began and ended with amazing versions of toro, the uni was perfect, and every other dish mixed the perfect amount of creativity and simplicity that made this one of the best meals I've had in NY.

Was a bit disappointed with the food here. We got the $175 tasting menu. Besides a few dishes that stood out, there was nothing really extraordinary about it. At these price points, Sushi Nakazawa is by far the better restaurant.

I don't give 5 stars often, unless it was truly a stellar meal. And of course it doesn't have to be a stuffy fancypants place to be stellar, although sometimes it is. Shuko was one of those upscale places and was truly, from the bottom of my heart, one of the best meals I've ever had. It's so badass that the door isn't even marked- it's this elite club that you enter because you know about it already. I got the omakase menu, every bite was carefully prepared in front of my eyes before being placed on my little stone tray and then popped into my mouth. It was as if centuries of preparation and thought had gone into the making of each bite; the culture and technique behind the assembly of the sushi, the flavor and texture profiles, the quality of the ingredients... I think when I went through that unmarked black door, I went to Narnia and then reemerged into the mundane world upon exit. Sake was phenomenal. I tasted everything that the sommelier (sakelier? sake master?) was describing. Service was awesome and very pleasant, we had a blast with the bartender. If you can get a res and have the cash to finance, go to shuko. If not, picture how the gods eat and you got yourself a fair approximation of this meal

Menu choice: Kaiseki

Food thoughts:
1- Mochi with pistactio - Bland, taste like rice with salt and shiso. 
2- Dungeness crab salad - This was okay. Too much focus on asethetics and no wow in flavor.
3-Toro and caviar - Disgusting. Extremely fishy and texture is very mushy.
4-Salmon and trout roe- Butchered. A nice piece of salmon can justify itself on it's own. Why throw in so much un-necessary components? Tempura flakes? Left a foul taste in my mouth
5-Lobster and bacon salad - Why? Lobster slapped on with fat? Bacon chunks are too think. Fat should have been rendered and bacon should be crispy. Bacon was too over powering and did not work with lobster. Plate looks like a mess.
6-Squab - why aren't there grill marks or more smokey flavor? Tasted like the meat was boiled.
7- Sushi pieces - delicate fish, but why put soy sauce on the fish and not let it stand out on it's own? Fish is such a delicacy. 
8- Desserts - shaved ice and bayleaf ice cream with apple pie. There's nothing special about these desserts and thought the shaved ice was too sweet. Bay leaf ice cream? Gross. Apple pie looked extremely messy, apples were not baked well. No eye in detail for this dish.

Service: 
Waiter was friendly, polite, and attentive. Sommelier did an excellent job with pairing the wine with the course, by far the best part of the expierence.

Atmosphere:
Felt that it was a place trying too hard to be relaxed by playing rap music but had such an up-tight rigid atmosphere. Not the most inviting restaurant. You will be sized up.

There was no inspiration that came from this experience. So many things did not work and in my perspective it seemed like they are trying to be something they are not. It shows in the food and employees. Don't get me wrong, I am not suggesting people should not try. I firmly believe people need to have their own experience and come to their own conclusion. For me, food could use some work.

It took me a while to find, but I'm glad I did, very discreet place. Walking in I loved the bar style restaurant! Very clean and welcoming. Hi Jerrad

So much smaller than the Hampton's Shuko

I'm a huge fan of great vibes while dining. The playlist played Jay Z, Biggie Smalls, Yezzy, A$AP, Adele, Justin and more loved it!!! Loud enough to vibe out, but able to hear your guests convo. 

Chefs Jimmy, Kim and Nick are the best! They made sure my date and I were welcomed and ready to enjoy great food!  Cheers 

We opted for the full tasting menu. Absolutely no complaints, chef kept the food coming my fav, Toro Tartare with Caviar, scallop cauliflower and sushi Omakase. Very warm and settling dishes. All prepared in my face. 

Great presentation 

Staff are great anything we need they were there before we could ask. 

Enough room for desert... I'm not a cake pie eater but it smelled astonishing! 

A bit pricy but worth it all. I do recommend this place you won't be disappointed! 

Best Japanese spot in town 
Check it out!!!!

I'm generally not the type of person who would post negative/critical Yelp views on restaurants.  However, today's dining experience (Tues 7/21/15) at Shuko has been so disappointing to the point where I felt it was a disservice to my conscience and my fellow patrons if I were not to finally sign up for Yelp and post my honest thoughts on my dining experience.

By way of background, my partner and I have been to Shuko's predecessor, Neta, a few times before.  Tonight, despite our 730pm seating right in right in front of Nick Kim, we were never greeted, and were never acknowledged by Nick.  Fine; we were not regulars by any definition, so why should our presence be validated?  By the third piece of the omakase course however, I took it upon myself to proactively say -- 'Hey, you're Nick, right?  We came to your former restaurant Neta a few times; we loved the tuna piece, and we decided we should come by to try your new restaurant'.  He responded with a disinterested and terse 'oh?  yeah that was good huh?' in a cold, monotonous manner that you wouldn't even expect from a novice chef, much less from one that would seemingly receive the type of favorable 'independent' reviews that he had.  Nick didn't utter anything else during our dinner.

Throughout our omakase dinner, we were served our pieces by his partner, Jimmy Lau.  We were disappointed by every single piece.  By way of background, my partner and I have sampled some of the finest sushi establishments in the world, ranging from Nakazawa and Yasuda in New York to Jiro and Nakamura in Tokyo to Sushi Shikon in Hong Kong.  This fell extremely, extremely far from any of those establishments.  In fact, I don't think this place is much better than your usual neighborhood Hatsuhana or Sushi Hakata establishment.

Almost all of the pieces were overpowered by the wasabi, and the rice was disturbingly inconsistent (either too hot and sticky, or cold and sticky).  As an aside, these were by far the smallest sushi pieces I've ever had.  Clearly Nick/Jimmy are looking out more for their profit margins than for their customers' experiences.

The lack of service/customer attentiveness could not be emphasized more.  As aforementioned, Nick showed a callous disregard to our patronage, despite my volunteering the fact that we were previous patrons to Neta.
